title: Best way to include a vignette in the package but not in the website?
description:
The [docs](https://pkgdown.r-lib.org/articles/pkgdown.html) describe how to include a vignette in the website but not in the package.

title: replay_html has problems when dealing with user defined S3 classes in @examples
description:
It is a bit hard for me to provide a reprex, but I will try to describe the problem as accurately as possible.
It seems rather simple anyways.

I am working on a package that deals with year-quarter dates. I have a roxygen block like this, where `date_y()` is a constructor for a custom s3 class for years:

```
#' [...]
#' @examples
#' date_y(2013)
```
If I run pkgdown::build_site (dev version, ‘1.0.0.9000’) I get:
```
Error in UseMethod("replay_html", x) : 
  no applicable method for 'replay_html' applied to an object of class "c('date_y', 'date_xx', 'integer')"
```

I do have proper `format()` and `print()` methods defined for `date_y` Objects. The problem described above does not occur if I change my @example to:
```
#' [...]
#' @examples
#' as.character(date_y(2013))
```

I havent looked to much in the internals of pkgdown, but maybe it makes sense to define a `replay_html.default()` like `replay_html.character(format(x))` or `replay_html.character(capture.output(print(x)))`?

title: Add RStudio hyperlink to generated files
Inconsistent naming of the configuration file in documentation
description:
The `pkgdown` documentation alternately refers to the configuration file as `_pkgdown.yml` or `_pkgdown.yaml`.  This might be a negligible annoyance if either extension could be used in all instances.  But as it stands now, the `.yaml` extension can only be used when the configuration file appears at the top level; files called `pkgdown/_pkgdown.yaml` or `inst/_pkgdown.yaml` will be silently ignored.  (I spend not a little time wondering why my `pkgdown/_pkgdown.yaml` wasn't working as expected.)

My recommendation would be the following:

1. Modify the `pkgdown_config_path` function so that `_pkgdown.yaml` can be used in every context in which `_pkgdown.yml` can currently be used.

2. Change all references in the documentation that mention `_pkgdown.yaml` to refer to `_pkgdown.yml` instead.  The _Introduction to pkgdown_ (_Get started_) vignette can include a footnote or parenthetical remark that extension `.yaml` may be used instead of `.yml` (just as it mentions in footnote 1 that the configuration file can be placed in the `inst` directory or in a `pkgdown` directory instead of at the top level).

3. Alternatively, do _not_ do recommendation 1 and instead have a footnote that reads something like this: "Note that for backward compatibility, the configuration file may be named `_pkgdown.yaml` instead of `pkgdown.yml`, _but only if the configuration file is placed in the top level package directory!_

title: Using library or require in an example inside \dontrun may cause an error
description:
To illustrate this problem, suppose we want to give an example using `deSolve` but don't want to make it a package requirement.  We might add something like this to the `\examples{ ... }` section of one of the `man` files:
```
\dontrun{
  library("deSolve")

  [ ... some code that uses deSolve ...]
}
```
If we don't actually have `deSolve` installed, `R CMD check` won't complain, but trying to build the `pkgdown` documentation gives rise to an error like
```
x Failed to parse Rd in system_derivatives.Rd
ℹ there is no package called ‘deSolve’
Caused by error in `loadNamespace()`:
! there is no package called ‘deSolve’ 

Execution halted
```

This certainly isn't expected!

It's not a huge problem—one can simply use fully-qualified function names, e.g. `deSolve::lsodes`, instead of calling the `library` function.  Alternatively, one could (again, leaving out the `library()` call) simply include a comment to the user who may wish to try the example saying that the example assumes that `deSolve` has been loaded and attached.  Nevertheless, it's disconcerting, to say the least, to get an error message from code that is supposedly "not run."

title: pkgdown tries to load namespace of package in unevaluated code
description:
The rsample package has the [output of a reprex in its README](https://rsample.tidymodels.org/). This decision was originally made because we don't want to include those packages as dependencies; they are not needed for anything except the demo in the README. 

- In older versions of pkgdown, this worked and that chunk was not evaluated. 
- In the newest version of pkgdown released yesterday, it looks like pkgdown attempts to load these packages and [we get an error](https://github.com/tidymodels/rsample/runs/7047333134?check_suite_focus=true#step:6:84):

> Error in loadNamespace(name) : there is no package called ‘mlbench’

As a temporary fix, I have added this package to `Config/Needs/website:`, which is fine, I guess. It was surprising, though, since this is in an unevaluated bit of markdown. What do you all think about this? Do you have a recommended solution for us?

However, if I use `pkgdown::build_article()`, then the class "my-class" is not applied to the code chunk and therefore the CSS is in the article but useless.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/52219252/175987421-f3ee9643-9002-48a9-9587-6e2d17489ad7.png)

`build_article()` documentation says that output formats in the YAML are not considered and the vignette is rendered with `rmarkdown::html_document` (which works correctly for applying the custom class), but nothing is said about the chunk option `class.source`. (I tried with `pkgdown` devel version)

---

title: topics cannot be excluded from reference index sections
description:
The documentation on topic matching says:

> Use a leading '-' to remove topics from a section, e.g. '-topic_name', '-starts_with("foo")'.

AFAIK, this is to allow for exclusion of specific topics in one set of references, for example:
```yaml
- contents:
  - has_keyword("datasets")
  - -foodata
```
This has worked in version 1.6.1 but it no longer does as from 2.0.0 -- most likely because of the changes in #1664. Topics are no longer selected based on the whole pattern vector (`select_topics(section$contents, pkg$topics)`, but one-by-one (`purrr::imap(section$contents, content_info, pkg = pkg, section = index)`). The above exclusion pattern actually leads to the inclusion of all topics.

Test code:
```R
ref <- list(
  list(contents = c("matches('[ab]')", "-b")),  # only a
  list(contents = c("b", "c", "?", "e"))        # all but a
)
meta <- list(reference = ref)
pkg <- as_pkgdown(test_path("assets/reference"), override = meta)
lapply(data_reference_index(pkg)$rows, `[[`, "names")
```

Observed result (in 2.0.2):
```
[[1]]
   a.Rd    b.Rd    c.Rd    e.Rd help.Rd 
    "a"     "b"     "c"     "e"     "?" 

[[2]]
   b.Rd    c.Rd help.Rd    e.Rd 
    "b"     "c"     "?"     "e" 
```

Expected result (as in 1.6.1):
```
[[1]]
a.Rd 
 "a" 

[[2]]
   b.Rd    c.Rd help.Rd    e.Rd 
    "b"     "c"     "?"     "e" 
```

title: Changes in R-4.2 can break loading of yml configs
description:
Just a heads-up that there are some small changes in R-4.2 that may cause bugs in the loading of yml configs. For example:

```r
❯ R-4.1 -q -e 'intersect(list(), "foo")'
> intersect(list(), "foo")
character(0)

❯ R-4.2 -q -e 'intersect(list(), "foo")'
> intersect(list(), "foo")
list()
```

We started seeing this error with R-4.2 using our [ropensci pkgdown template](https://github.com/ropensci-org/rotemplate):

```
-- Building home ---------------------------------------------------------------
Error in components[left_comp] : invalid subscript type 'list'
```

The problem it turned out was that our template `pkgdown.yml` had this:

```yml
navbar:
  structure:
    left:  []
    right: [search, intro, reference, articles, tutorials, news, github]
```

Here `left:  []` is parsed as an empty `list()` which pkgdown then feeds to `intersect()`:

https://github.com/r-lib/pkgdown/blob/98d5a5c735eb244cb98b2e6bab1d54bb27c0af95/R/navbar.R#L54

Because of the behavioral change mentioned above, previously this would return a vector, but in R 4.2 it returns a list, causing type errors down the line.

title: fixed width htmlwidgets are displayed too large.
description:
This code:  https://github.com/r-lib/pkgdown/blob/98d5a5c735eb244cb98b2e6bab1d54bb27c0af95/R/pkgdown_print.R#L39
in `pkgdown_print.htmlwidget` is equivalent to

     x$width <- (x$width %||% settings$fig.width) * settings$dpi 

because the ` %||%` operator has higher precedence than `*`.  But for htmlwidgets, the width is specified in CSS units (defaulting to pixels), not inches, so really we want

    x$width <- x$width %||% (settings$fig.width * settings$dpi)

or the widget will be displayed too large.  (This is a somewhat rare occurence; most commonly `x$width` is `NULL`.)

To see this, put this example code in an Rd file:

    library(leaflet)
    m <- leaflet() %>% addTiles()
    m$width <- 200
    m$height <- 200
    m

The map will end up huge in `pkgdown`, while in most displays it's a small 200x200 pixels.  Setting the width to a character string including units should work, but gives `#> Error in x$width %||% settings$fig.width * settings$dpi: non-numeric argument to binary operator` in `build_reference`.

title: Enabling cross references and htmlwidgets together in >=v2.0.0
description:
The refactor of the `as_is` option in v2.0.0 broke the possibility of having htmlwidgets and custom output format used together (see https://github.com/r-lib/pkgdown/pull/1793#issuecomment-931752561).

title: Generic roxygen 7.2.0 code blocks not rendered in `pkgdown::build_site()`
Add possibility to add contents that are missing from previous reference sections
description:
At the moment, if you enable the reference: section, you are forced to curate the list completely manually. As far as I could see, there's no way to say "everything that has not been matched previously" so I can have an "other" section with everything else. Example:

```
reference:
- title: Object Constructors
  desc: Functions to create objects
  contents:
  - foo
  - bar

- title: Other
  desc: Other functions
  contents:
  - matches(".*")
```

using matches with the regexp will create indeed such section with everything, but foo and bar will appear both in the Object Constructor sections and in the Other sections.

What is needed is a function equivalent to matches() that matches every function that has not been selected previously, like `unmatched()` or something like that.

then the Rd is

```r
\figure{logo.png}{Package logo
blablablablablabla}
}
```

Which creates an error via

https://github.com/r-lib/pkgdown/blob/b273ac6e9057e5c5abcf45730e8f8770de0e890c/R/rd-html.R#L332

Should

A workaround is to write alternative text on one line in the roxygen2 tags.

title: Add support for GoatCounter and possibly other alternatives to Google Analytics
description:
As [requested by @hadley](https://github.com/r-lib/pkgdown/pull/1546#issuecomment-791929828), this issue is supposed to be the place to discuss the addition of GoatCounter and possibly other alternatives to Google Analytics.

### What is GoatCounter

GoatCounter's [self-portrayal](https://www.goatcounter.com/):

> GoatCounter is an open source web analytics platform available as a hosted service (free for non-commercial use) or self-hosted app. It aims to offer easy to use and meaningful privacy-friendly web analytics as an alternative to Google Analytics or Matomo.

Personally, I think it's awesome. It's simple but works well for me.

### What's the competition

To my knowledge, there aren't many free _hosted_ web analytics platforms that meet all of the three criteria below:

- pre-hosted service free for non-commercial use
- open source and thus self-hostable
- privacy-aware, i.e. it does _by design_ neither track visitors with unique identifiers, nor store any personal data or even rely on cookies – so there's ([almost certainly](https://www.goatcounter.com/gdpr)) no legal requirement to show any of these ugly and annoying privacy/cookie consent banners in EU jurisdiction.

[**Google Analytics**](https://marketingplatform.google.com/about/analytics/) which pkgdown already supports does offer more powerful visitor tracking features and stuff but only meets one of the above criteria: It's free as a hosted service. But it's not open source and is owned by the world's largest data kraken.

The most popular alternative for people wanting to be in complete control of the gathered analytics data seems to be [**Matomo**](https://matomo.org/). It does meet two of the above criteria but its hosted service is not free (not even for non-commercial users). Which probably will be a major obstacle for most pkgdown sites.

Another interesting alternative is [**counter.dev**](https://counter.dev/). It actually seems to meet all the three criteria above, too, but I haven't really tested it yet. AFAICT it shares a lot of similarities with GoatCounter but has some notable [design differences](https://github.com/ihucos/counter.dev#how-can-it-be-free), especially:

> - We only track the first page the user views, this is again more privacy friendly and additionally also results in substantial less HTTP requests the server has to handle. As a result of this strategy, Counter is able to show top landing pages but not top pages.
> - While most other analytics solutions provide the tracking script as an externally hosted file, we use a small inline tracking script. Doing so mitigates the need to host and serve such a script and avoids any otherwise necessary efforts to secure such an externally hosted script, which would have to be trusted by all our users.

Adding support for counter.dev to pkgdown would be _very_ easy.

title: rmarkdown breaks heading anchors for Pandoc > 2.8
description:

Therefore it removes the "hasAnchor" class that's needed to have working heading anchors. :cry: 

I noticed the missing anchors in articles as I was working on #1536 but it's unrelated. Locally I use Pandoc 2.11.12. The preview of that PR doesn't show the problem, nor the pkgdown dev/production websites, as the GHA workflow uses an older Pandoc version.

cc @cderv 

We could remove the dependency in one of the HTML tweaks, if a fix doesn't happen upstream (and if a fix happens upstream, we'll have to increase the rmarkdown minimal version in DESCRIPTION so this issue is useful here).

title: How to update the site for released version of a package
description:
I'm using

```
development:
  mode: auto
```

more often these days, which means there's two version of the site, e.g. one for the released version of the package https://gmailr.r-lib.org and another for the development version of the package https://gmailr.r-lib.org/dev/.

But sometimes you need to update the released site, even though the package version in current source has already advanced to a development version. My most recent example was needing to backport some documentation changes and pkgdown config fixes to gmailr's released site.

This issue is a reminder to us to document how to do this.

**UPDATE**: I gradually realized that our existing pkgdown GHA workflow is capable of doing this. You just need to create a branch that reflects the source state you want to pkgdown-render from ~and push a tag pointing to that ref. I'm going to delete or hide the notes about my journey to this realization~. *Update: read on for what to do with this branch.*

title: deploy_to_branch: is there a conflict between clean and lazy?
description:
In [`pkgdown::deploy_to_branch`](https://pkgdown.r-lib.org/reference/deploy_to_branch.html), one of the function options is `clean` (default is `TRUE`): ["Clean all files from old site."](https://github.com/r-lib/pkgdown/blob/main/R/clean.R) The `deploy_to_branch` function also takes additional arguments, that are passed to `build_site`. One of these arguments is `lazy`: "If TRUE, will only rebuild articles and reference pages if the source is newer than the destination." 

I am trying to use `deploy_to_branch` with Github Actions to rebuild the site on certain pushes. However, the vignettes in my package cannot run on Github's VM (restricted access to data, for example). I wanted to build the vignettes locally, and then push the `doc` folder and have it be deployed with `deploy_to_branch`. I was under the impression that setting the options `clean = FALSE` and `lazy = TRUE` would allow for that (not rebuilding vignettes), but the `deploy_to_branch` still tries to rebuild all vignettes (I manually checked that all files under vignettes/ were older than their builds in docs/articles). 

Is there a way to use `deploy_to_branch` without rebuilding vignettes if they are already up to date?

Thanks for helping!!!!!

title: Create new `use_git_ignore_template` based on toptal.com (former gitignore.io)
description:
`usethis` may benefit a lot from the API provided by https://www.toptal.com/developers/gitignore

For example,
`use_git_ignore_template(c("linux", "macos", "windows", "r"))`, would translate to the API response of:
https://www.toptal.com/developers/gitignore/api/linux,macos,windows,r

As you see the response link, the entries of line 2 could be parsed and recycled if a users wants to modify this.

My usual .gitignore has the following pattern:
```
# my stuff
raw/
subjectdata/
token.R

# gitignore.io part (DO NOT MODIFY HERE USE use_git_ignore_template() to update the components below)
# Created by https://www.toptal.com/developers/gitignore/api/linux,macos,windows,r
# Edit at https://www.toptal.com/developers/gitignore?templates=linux,macos,windows,r

### Linux ###
*~

# temporary files which can be created if a process still has a handle open of a deleted file
.fuse_hidden*
# ...
```

title: Institutional logo not rendered
description:
I have the institutional logo indicated in `_pkgdown.yml`:

https://github.com/maialab/grantham/blob/091bd0b97cad9a1eaad26c88fdda0aa241b5a071/_pkgdown.yml#L13-L15

It is located in the source here: https://maialab.org/grantham/reference/figures/cintesis.svg.

title: How to specify path in `_pkgdown.yml`'s `html` parameter
description: For a minimal reprex, see this package website: https://indrajeetpatil.github.io/minimalReprex/ The logo is rendered correctly in the footer only on the [homepage](https://indrajeetpatil.github.io/minimalReprex/): ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/11330453/148369928-856eac0d-eaae-44eb-b515-75c4c0182c08.png) But not on any other [page](https://indrajeetpatil.github.io/minimalReprex/reference/index.html): ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/11330453/148369998-c86fa634-b4ed-4541-b067-3f5eae745af8.png) I understand that anywhere other than `index.html`, this relative path `reference/figures/hu.png` fails, and that's what creates this issue. But I am not sure what the alternative way of specifying this path in `_pkgdown.yaml` is so that the funder logo will be available across all pages: ```yaml authors: Harvard University: href: "Harvard University" html: "" ``` P.S. I also checked out `{tidytemplate}`, since RStudio logo is rendered successfully across all pages of respective websites, but its [yaml](https://github.com/tidyverse/tidytemplate/blob/main/_pkgdown.yml) didn't provide any clues.

title: Confusing error message
description:
I just inherited gmailr and found that its site hasn't been building for a while.

The problem was an empty item:

https://github.com/r-lib/gmailr/commit/d5d90f30cdf23a44cbaa8fefb22c48370c015f28#diff-f5f791eb2285a738ec729c44088e49a60ddf355eb479fb1fb5df7fcea4fea2e8L75

but the pkgdown error message is a bit misleading. I figure the error with previous pkgdown isn't that interesting, but you can see it [in GHA logs](https://github.com/r-lib/gmailr/runs/4355063527?check_suite_focus=true#step:6:42).

With current dev pkgdown, the error is

```
-- Building function reference -------------------------------------------------
Error : Item 1 in section 8 in reference in '_pkgdown.yml' must be a character.
ℹ You might need to add '' around e.g. - 'N' or - 'off'.
Error: callr subprocess failed: Item 1 in section 8 in reference in '_pkgdown.yml' must be a character.
ℹ You might need to add '' around e.g. - 'N' or - 'off'.
```

This bit was accurate: `section 8 in reference in '_pkgdown.yml'`.

But this was wrong: `Item 1 in ...` (or else maybe I misunderstand what Item 1 refers to).

And this hints feels very specific, but it's also sort of a misdiagnosis:
```
ℹ You might need to add '' around e.g. - 'N' or - 'off'.`
```

title: A small tabset oddity
description:
Thanks to @maelle (#1694) tabsets work fantastically in vignettes which is really great. They should also work (and mostly do) in other places like the home page from `readme.md` But I'm noticing one oddity. I can't quite tell if this is a bootstrap problem or something else going on.

I made a basic [example package showing this](https://jonkeane.github.io/simple-package/index.html). By default the R tab is selected, but if you scroll past it (on both safari and chrome), the css features that show that it's selected (rounded box, grey background, different color type) disappear (though the tab content remains). I also included an identical tabset in [the vignette](https://jonkeane.github.io/simple-package/articles/a-vignette.html) which works just fine and one can scroll past it without changing the selection indications.

https://github.com/jonkeane/simple-package has the source of the simple package.

title: Support prose in examples
description:
In `reprex::reprex()` and `knitr::spin()`, roxygen formatted comments get rendered as prose. 
It would be great if pkgdown did the same for examples.

Concretely, I'm proposing users could write something like:
```R
#' A title
#'
#' @export
#' @examples
#' #' This gets rendered as prose
#' this_is_rendered_as_monospaced_code <- fn()
#' 
#' #' This also gets rendered as prose
#' this_is_also_rendered_as_monospaced_code <- fn()
fn <- function() { }
```

title: Depends on withr >= 2.4.0
description:
## Issue
pkgdown fails to work if a version of the package `withr` is installed which does not export the function `local_seed` as it is called in function `examples_env`. See [this changelog](https://github.com/r-lib/withr/releases/tag/v2.4.0). 
## Fix
This could be fixed by adding `withr (>= 2.4.0)` to the DESCRIPTION file.

title: doi: auto-linkage breaks markdown links
description:
My R package contains a [README.md](https://github.com/ms609/Ternary#readme) file with the string
`doi:[10.5281/zenodo.1068996](https://dx.doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.1068996)`, formatted as necessary for the link to resolve in the README page on GitHub.

But when this page is [rendered by pkgdown](https://ms609.github.io/Ternary/dev/), I see:

[doi:\[10.5281/zenodo.1068996](https://doi.org/[10.5281/zenodo.1068996)](https://dx.doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.1068996).

Apparently the `[` is being interpreted as part of a DOI and pkgdown is trying to auto-link it.

Could the regexp used to auto-link DOIs be expanded to be more precise, e.g. `doi:10\.\d+`?

description:
The [build home](https://github.com/r-lib/pkgdown/blob/e1e46f2e13c7efdb17bc4eae40bc3779c2b0b517/R/build-home.R#L64) file has: 

> `@section Images and figures`:  If you want to include images in your `README.md`, they must be stored somewhere in the package so that they can be displayed on the CRAN website. The best place to put them is `man/figures`. If you are generating figures with R Markdown, make sure you set up `fig.path` as followed:

It looks like the site pages convert or copy the `man` directory to one called `reference` for the README file, but not for articles. 

For example, the [`rules` vignette](https://github.com/tidymodels/rules/blob/4af59ef30b5dca9556f1ad1a36f4a57b4cab7672/vignettes/Cubist-and-RuleFit.Rmd#L32) does this and results in a broken link. title: Font is wrong
description:
I'm going to open and close this in rapid succession, but seems like a good gotcha to document.

When getting the gmailr site back online, I quickly got to 99% success but the requested fonts weren't being used.

The answer was that there was no `.nojekyll` file in the `gh-pages` branch. And Jekyll won’t distribute directories (or files) that start with a `_`, which is true of the directories where the fonts live.

So the fonts looked correct locally, where no Jekyll is involved. But the fonts were wrong in GitHub Pages, which does involve Jekyll, unless you specifically tell it to stand down via `.nojekyll`.

If you use our current processes to build and deploy a pkgdown site, you will have a `.nojekyll` file. But due to the peculiar history and process of what I was doing, I didn't have that file and it needed to be added manually.

e.g. https://tidytemplate.tidyverse.org/articles/headings.html#heading-4b

title: Eliminate duplicates within (sub)sections
description:
The reference now allows duplicates so a single topic can appear in multiple sections. Before this change, duplicates would be removed. While it is useful to allow a topic to appear in multiple sections, it seems they should still be removed within sections, which is no longer the case.

This is mostly problematic when aliases are included in the reference as this now causes duplicate entries. The current behaviour is not backward compatible and is also a bit impractical, as one must now know about aliases, choose which alias to include in the reference, and double check the reference for duplicate entries.

title: Duplicated reference pages
description:
Package `rgl` has a single help page documenting five different functions.  The `_pkgdown.yml` entries are separate:

```
- subtitle: Primitive shapes
- contents:
  - points3d
  - lines3d
  - segments3d
  - triangles3d
  - quads3d
```

but in fact there's just one page referenced.  When I did the last release of `rgl` back in August, the reference page combined all of these into one entry.  See https://dmurdoch.github.io/rgl/reference/index.html , which has

```
Primitive shapes
--
points3d() lines3d() segments3d() triangles3d() quads3d() | Add primitive shape

```

Using today's devel build of `pkgdown`, I get duplicated entries.  See https://dmurdoch.github.io/rgl/dev/reference/index.html , which has

```
Primitive shapes
--
points3d() lines3d() segments3d() triangles3d() quads3d() | Add primitive shape
points3d() lines3d() segments3d() triangles3d() quads3d() | Add primitive shape
points3d() lines3d() segments3d() triangles3d() quads3d() | Add primitive shape
points3d() lines3d() segments3d() triangles3d() quads3d() | Add primitive shape
points3d() lines3d() segments3d() triangles3d() quads3d() | Add primitive shape
```

It is recognizing the duplication by putting all the function names on each line, but forgetting to remove the unnecessary copies.

description:
Roles [without a translation](https://github.com/r-lib/pkgdown/blob/3912737f46bf1f9f04ce59ee333b685d7bff599f/R/build-home-authors.R#L198-L211) appear as `NA` in the author section of the sidebar, e.g.

``` r
pkgdown:::role_lookup(c("res", "ccp", "aut"))
#> [1] NA       NA       "author"
```

`"ccp"` (Conceptor) is a role that happens to be used in a couple packages I maintain; I noticed `"res"` (Researcher) when searching GitHub to gauge how widely `"ccp"` is used. Both seem to have enough usage to warrant a translation.

Whether or not you decide to add those two roles to the role lookup list, it might be useful to remove `NA` values or to fall back on the English term from `utils:::MARC_relator_db` for roles not explicitly translated.

title: Custom templates based on the `content-article` template
description:
Somewhat building on the feature request in #1893, it'd be useful to advanced users of pkgdown to be able to create additional content layout templates. 

I imagine the source content would be written, stored, and processed in all the same places and ways that articles are currently, but instead of using the `content-article.html`, they could use an alternative template chosen via an option in the YAML frontmatter of the article.

As a hypothetical example, the article stored in `vignettes/gallery.Rmd` might start with

```markdown
---
title: Gallery of Examples
content_type: gallery
---
```

that would cause `render_page_html()` to find and use a `content-gallery.html` template rather than `content-article.html`, throwing an error if an appropriate content template can't be found.

(The `content_type` YAML key is just a first draft name suggestion, of course.)

title: Allow templates to be provided in the `pkgdown/` directory
description:
A package author might want to make limited changes to a parent pkgdown template, or perhaps provide an additional customization for a template.

Much like hugo accepts custom layout templates at the site level that take precedence over the global theme's layout, I'd like to propose that templates in a `pkgdown/templates` directory in a package's project take precedence over the templates provided by the template defined in `_pkgdown.yml` or those provided by `pkgdown` directly. The end result is that it becomes easier to make small modifications without needing the additional infrastructure of a package or without having to make upstream modifications to the template package.

If this seems reasonable, I'd be happy to provide a PR. I have a working local implementation that adds `path(pkg$src_path, "pkgdown", "templates")` to the front of the [`template_candidates()`](https://github.com/pkgdown/pkgdown/blob/3912737f46bf1f9f04ce59ee333b685d7bff599f/R/templates.R#L33) paths here:

https://github.com/r-lib/pkgdown/blob/3912737f46bf1f9f04ce59ee333b685d7bff599f/R/templates.R#L39-L42

Since `template_candidates()` doesn't take `pkg` as an argument, we'd need to update the function signature and ensure that `src_path` is passed down through [`find_template()`](https://github.com/r-lib/pkgdown/blob/3912737f46bf1f9f04ce59ee333b685d7bff599f/R/templates.R#L1-L5) from its calling functions, much like how `templates_dir` is handled currently.

title: Unnest articles in the `vignettes/articles` directory
description:
Storing non-vignette articles in the `vignettes/articles` directory is a convenient way to isolate articles and assets that shouldn't be included in the installed package. It's also the default behavior of `usethis::use_article()` — to place new articles in a `vignettes/articles` directory and to ensure an entry exists in `.Rbuildignore` to ignore the articles directory.

The downside of this approach is that pkgdown moves articles to `<root>/articles/<path inside vignettes>`, resulting in URLs like `<root>/articles/articles/examples.html`.

One example:

- pkgdown: https://reprex.tidyverse.org/articles/articles/rtf.html
- source: [vignettes/articles/rtf.Rmd](https://github.com/tidyverse/reprex/blob/master/vignettes/articles/rtf.Rmd)

I understand that this is mostly cosmetic and that it might not be desirable to change the default behavior since many public URLs probably include `articles/articles`. Perhaps new behavior of moving these articles to `articles/` could be opt-in behind a config option with a default value that might change in the future. Or maybe the new redirects feature could be used to mitigate the downstream issues of simplifying the URL.

One way in which this isn't just cosmetic is that, as a user following the lead from `use_article()`, there's a sense that `vignettes/articles/` is _special_. For the most part, wherever pkgdown handles links I wouldn't have noticed the URL, but I had a hard time anticipating the final path of shared assets and was surprised to discover the extra `articles/`.

title: Tabset processing removes HTML from tab title
description: It's not completely uncommon to have HTML in a heading that becomes a tabset tab name. Here are two examples, one using inline code and the other adding an icon to the tab name. In both cases, by creating the title name from `xml2::xml_text()` the tab buttons end up losing the HTML. ``` r pkgload::load_all() #> ℹ Loading pkgdown html <- markdown_to_html(" ## Tabset {.tabset} ### Tab 1 `with_code` {#toc-1} Contents 1 ### Tab 2 {#toc-2} Contents 2 ") tweak_tabsets(html) print_xpath_html_and_text <- function(x, xpath) { x <- xml2::xml_find_first(x, xpath) print(as.character(x)) xml2::xml_text(x) } ``` The first tab should have `with_code` as `with_code` ```r print_xpath_html_and_text(html, "//*[@id = 'toc-1-tab']") #> [1] "" #> [1] "Tab 1 with_code" ``` and the second tab should include the `` element. ```r print_xpath_html_and_text(html, "//*[@id = 'toc-2-tab']") #> [1] "" #> [1] "Tab 2" ```

title: Translation cause a crash of R in some functions when doing YAML conversion
description:
This happens with last pkgdown version which include translation, and I believe this is due to the new translation system

As I am running on a French computer, any work I do with pkgdown will now apply translation. It will sometimes add accentuated characters like `References` -> `Référence`.

`template_navbar()` will create a list of component of the navbar, but will now translate them. So for example, `menu$reference$text` is now `Référence`. The crash happens from `navbar_components()` in the `print_yaml` call
https://github.com/r-lib/pkgdown/blob/6a412e3a9d2d12d43e6b24eb25b97633ec350cda/R/navbar.R#L93-L116

This is because `yaml::as.yaml(menu)` will cause a crash. This is a known issue in `yaml` R package I believe 
https://github.com/viking/r-yaml/issues/90

The encoding of `menu$reference$text` is unknown. Setting it to UTF8 (`enc2utf8(menu$reference$text)` solves the issue. 
Maybe it should be encoded to utf8 all the time ? (in `tr_`) ?

I think pkgdown will need to deal with this somehow in all the function where translated word can end up into YAML. 

I did not come up with a reprex specific to pkgdown, as the reprex is the one for `yaml` package issue.

title: Move `master` branch to `main`
description:
The `master` branch of this repository will soon be renamed to `main`, as part of a coordinated change across several GitHub organizations (including, but not limited to: [tidyverse](https://github.com/tidyverse), [r-lib](https://github.com/r-lib), [tidymodels](https://github.com/tidymodels), and [sol-eng](https://github.com/sol-eng)). We anticipate this will happen by the end of September 2021.

That will be preceded by a release of the [usethis package](https://usethis.r-lib.org), which will gain some functionality around detecting and adapting to a renamed default branch. There will also be a blog post at the time of this `master` --> `main` change.

The purpose of this issue is to:

* Help us firm up the list of targetted repositories
* Make sure all maintainers are aware of what's coming
* Give us an issue to close when the job is done
* Give us a place to put advice for collaborators re: how to adapt

*message id: euphoric_snowdog*

title: More flexibility in dev-vs-"stable" version numbering
description:

title: "Topics missing from index:"  incorrect?
description:
I'm writing a package to work with glTF files, importing them into `rgl` and exporting `rgl` scenes to that format.  When I build [the web site](https://dmurdoch.github.io/rgl2gltf/dev) using `pkgdown::build_site()` on a local copy, I get a warning:

The `as.rglscene` function is a generic from `rgl` that I have imported and re-exported.  It is mentioned on a help page listing the generics like that (there are two others, `plot3d` and `as.mesh3d`).  It is the only one for which a warning pops up.

What index is it missing from?  Why is it being treated differently than the other two?  

In case this goes away, I am using the latest pkgdown ( cd888be ) and it happens with rgl2gltf from here:  https://github.com/dmurdoch/rgl2gltf/tree/3f8f95b08e63bf6a111541b13f40ac55f366fb9c .

description:

The final 30 versions then come into view, but if I click on one of them that's not right near the bottom, I lose them again.

This is using Bootstrap 3 with the Github devel version of pkgdown, but the same issue occurs with CRAN pkgdown.  For my first attempt with Bootstrap 4 I saw the same thing, but after updating all packages to devel versions, the contents listing has disappeared completely (at least with `pkgdown::build_news()`).

I think the solution would be to make the contents listing scrollable.

out$name (`actual`) not equal to "test-1" (`expected`).

`actual`:           
`expected`: "test-1"

On cursory inspection of the code, it wasn't obvious to me why this
- should be skipped on local machines (in addition to existing `skip_*()`s)
- would fail.

I'm assuming all CI will skip this because of missing rsconnect and accounts.

I don't know enough about tutorials to fix this or even know whether it's a real bug or just a test but.
Adds a bit of friction for contributors (I always freak out a bit when my local `test()` run fails when I contribute).

description:
Since #1313 the docs mention one can use `_site.yml`.

However @cderv explained to me that it's more logical and simple to use `_output.yml`. Logical because the site config is for websites, and simple because you can omit the "output" key.

E.g. `_output.yml` can be

```yaml
html_document:
  toc: true
  toc_float: true
  number_sections: false
  theme: flatly
```

title: Support the use of as_is and _site.yml?
description:
Via https://github.com/r-lib/pkgdown/issues/1749#issuecomment-903886379

In the case where `as_is` is TRUE, currently pkgdown will try to extract the output name from the frontmatter but when one uses `_site.yml` there is no output name in the frontmatter.

AFAICT `_site.yml` is supported by rmarkdown, not directly by pkgdown. Here is where rmarkdown extracts the output format information from `_site.yml`: https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/blob/0af6b3556adf6e393b2da23c66c695724ea7bd2d/R/output_format.R#L493

title: Output plots in help files are incorrect when a legend is added
description:
I'm using `pkgdown` to generate a website for my package. One of the `plot()` functions in my package adds a legend to the side of the plot (in the margin). When running it in R (and outputting the plot to a file) it works just fine. But when the plots are created for the 'Examples' section of the help files, the legend is not being placed correctly.

I've come up with a reproducible example. It uses a very simple function that adds a legend to an existing plot, using the user coordinates (from `par("usr")`) to place the legend in the margin. After a lot of trial and error, I've found that the error seems to occur when `asp` and either `xlim` or `ylim` is set. The example makes a 2 x 2 plot grid showing the outputs with different parameters used for `plot()` and outputs it to a file - I dug through some of the package code (especially the `fig_save()` function in `R/figure.R`) and was able to derive the parameters being used when `pkgdown` makes the plots. I used these parameters to save the plot to a file, using the same graphics device as `pkgdown` (`ragg:agg_png()`). I should also note that I'm not setting any of the `figures:` parameters in `_pkgdown.yml`.

``` r
add_lgd <- function(){
  rast <- as.raster(hcl.colors(100))
  usr <- par("usr")
  rasterImage(rast, 
              xleft = usr[2],
              ybottom = usr[3], 
              xright = usr[2] + .2, 
              ytop = usr[4],
              xpd = TRUE)
}

ragg::agg_png("~/path/to/file/example.png", width = 1400, height = 866, res = 192, bg = NA)

par(mfrow = c(2,2))
plot(1,1, main = "default")
add_lgd()

plot(1,1, xlim = c(0,1), ylim = c(0,1), asp = 1, main = "xlim = c(0,1), ylim = c(0,1), asp = 1")
add_lgd()

plot(1,1, xlim = c(0,1), asp = 1, main = "xlim = c(0,1), asp = 1")
add_lgd()

plot(1,1, ylim = c(0,1), asp = 1, main = "ylim = c(0,1), asp = 1" )
add_lgd()

dev.off()
```

The output looks like this:

![example](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/7896671/135164688-a6ffc257-acf0-432e-bfb1-08e0aade79f3.png)

I put the example code in the `@examples` section of the Roxygen documentation of one my R files and removed the calls to `ragg::agg_png()` and `dev.off()`. I then used `pkgdown::build_site()` to build the website. Here's the image that `pkgdown` creates:

![plot-22](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/7896671/135165047-d42f4779-9004-431d-9aec-5c5ba5fff4ea.png)

As you can see, the legend bar is displayed differently than when I manually saved the plot to a file even though I used the same graphics device with the same parameter settings. In particular, when `ylim` and `asp` are set it the legend appears on top of the plot. I tried every combination of these parameters, and if `asp=1` is used without `xlim` and `ylim`, it works fine. And the same goes when I used `xlim` and/or `ylim` without `asp`.

I'm at a loss as to what's happening and how to fix it, although I'm guessing it has something to do with the fact that I'm using `par("usr")` to determine where to place the legend.

title: Function for building for github pages
description:
```R
build_site_github_pages <- function(pkg = ".", clean = TRUE) {
 pkg <- as_pkgdown(pkg, override = list(destination = dest_dir))

  if (clean) {
    rule("Cleaning files from old site", line = 1)
    clean_site(pkg)
  }

  build_site(pkg, devel = FALSE, preview = FALSE, install = FALSE, ...)
  build_github_pages(pkg)
  
  invisible()
}
```

Then we could refactor our [standard action](https://github.com/r-lib/actions/blob/master/examples/pkgdown-pak.yaml) to build and then deploy. So instead of:

```yaml
     - name: Build and deploy pkgdown site
        run: |
          git config --local user.name "$GITHUB_ACTOR"
          git config --local user.email "$GITHUB_ACTOR@users.noreply.github.com"
          Rscript -e 'pkgdown::deploy_to_branch(new_process = FALSE)'
```

We'd have something like:

```yaml
      - name: Build pkgdown site
        run: pkgdown::build_site_github_pages()
        shell: Rscript {0}

      - name: Deploy 🚀
        uses: JamesIves/github-pages-deploy-action@4.1.4
        with:
          folder: docs
```

Would you be open to creating a `manifest.json` file as part of `build_site()` or `deploy_to_branch()`?

My team and I heavily use RStudio Connect, and we love [Git-backed content](https://docs.rstudio.com/connect/user/git-backed/). Thanks to `pkgdown::deploy_to_branch()` and `usethis::use_github_action("pkgdown")`, it is almost trivially easy to continuously deploy a package site on Connect. My personal workaround is to run `build_site()` locally, run `rsconnect::writeManifest()` from inside `docs/`, then copy `manfiest.json` to `pkgdown/favicon/`. title: Logo is no longer displayed if SVG version is present
description:
`find_logo` preferentially finds an SVG logo, if present.

However, `copy_assets` always copies that logo file to a file called `package-logo.png`. This causes the browser to not render the logo at all, and no logo is displayed (Safari additionally displays a “missing image” placeholder).

The PNG version should probably be preferred, if present: it’s going to have been rendered from the SVG and is more portable (for instance, Inkscape by default includes text spans in SVGs without embedding the font, which will therefore render differently if the client hasn’t got the font installed). I’d submit a PR but I don’t actually know how to handle the SVG case: `package-logo.png` is currently hard-coded in multiple places. Should it be replaced by a function call? Or should pkgdown attempt to render the SVG into a PNG itself?

I think the break was introduced in #1584. That PR also makes the displayed logo smaller on *all* pages (including the homepage): 100px, instead of previously 120px (or whatever was specified), at least when using Bootstrap v4. Was this intentional?

Function reference: '\item's in \value{} should be formatted like those in \arguments{}
description:
For functions returning a list, the CRAN documentation guidelines recommend documentation of the form 

```
\item{comp_i}{Description of comp_i.}
```

for each component of the list in the `\value{}` section, exactly as in the `\arguments{}` section.  And if you open the documentation for such an entry in R or RStudio, the formatting will be consistent: the  `\value{}` section will look like the `\arguments{}` section.  In `pkgdown`, however (version 1.1.0), the two sections look different.  The list in the `\value{}` section is formatted like a list with headings, not like a section listing specific keywords in code.  It's a minor issue, but I thought it was worth pointing out.

By the way, this can be worked around in `pkgdown` by wrapping the list in a `\describe{}` environment, but then the documentation is no longer formatted correctly in R/RStudio.

Visually, this is what I'm talking about:

![1](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1858089/46086746-692e3780-c16e-11e8-8257-622b45f48d62.png)

The above line is inserted in the source of that page to give a simple example (https://github.com/GeoBosh/cvar/blob/master/R/cvar-package.R, lines 84, 88).  The references should also be in three separate paragraphs (since there are three references).

title: deploy_to_branch overwrites the current list of branches tracked
description:
Hi! I was trying to track down an issue with my `git fetch -a` command and I think it's due to the behaviour of this particular line in the deploy_to_branch function.

https://github.com/r-lib/pkgdown/blob/eae56f08694abebf93cdfc0dd8e9ede06d8c815f/R/deploy-site.R#L158

title: Support bookdown
description:
While writing a bunch of rich interlinked vignettes for vctrs, it made me wish I could write in bookdown instead. There would be a number of advantages to writing a book instead of vignettes:

* Built in linear flow
* Easier to link between pages
* Wouldn't bundle in package so don't need to worry about file size

I think it would be _relatively_ easy to support package "book" from pkgdown:

* We adopt a convention for the directory a bookdown site should live in (and provide a usethis helper to create the basic structure)

* We'd need to re-theme the output, probably by using the same approach we already do for Rmarkdown. Alternatively, we might need a completely new theme to replace gitbook.

* We'd add a new heading to the nav bar which would list all h1s from the book (and maybe, optionally, the h2s?)

title: pkgdown does not respect \dontshow
description:
`\dontshow` is standard syntax to suppress parts of the examples that should not be displayed in the documentation, but `pkgdown` ignores the tag and displays these anyway (understandable since pkgdown isn't running `LaTeX`, but you see my point).

I know `\dontshow` isn't commonly used, historically it would be used to hide test conditions where "examples" doubled as "unit-tests" (though there is a certain Knuth-ian literate programming flavor to having your tests sit next to your source-code).  I also find `\dontshow` preferable for setting things like environmental variables that are only relevant to meet CRAN requirements (i.e. not writing to disk outside temp storage), since it confuses some users to show examples that show commands writing to a temporary location on operations that intend to persist between sessions.  Anyway, a minor issue but I think it is worth noting.

title: Example registering globalCallingHandlers() causes build_reference() to fail
description:
# Problem

If a help example attempts to set a global calling handler, e.g. 

```r
\examples{
globalCallingHandlers(NULL)
}
```

then `pkgdown::build_reference()` will fail with
```
Error in globalCallingHandlers(NULL) : 
 should not be called with handlers on the stack
```


# Example

```sh
$ git clone https://github.com/HenrikBengtsson/teeny.git
$ cd teeny
$ git checkout pkgdown/globalCallingHandlers 
Branch 'pkgdown/globalCallingHandlers' set up to track remote branch 'pkgdown/globalCallingHandlers' from 'origin'.
Switched to a new branch 'pkgdown/globalCallingHandlers'

$ Rscript -e "pkgdown::build_reference()"
-- Building function reference -------------------------------------------------
Writing 'reference/index.html'
ℹ Loading teeny
Reading 'man/hello.Rd'
Error in globalCallingHandlers(NULL) : 
  should not be called with handlers on the stack
```


# Troubleshooting

I suspect this is because `build_reference()` runs the example code within a `tryCatch()`, in which one cannot register global calling handlers, e.g.

```r
tryCatch({
  globalCallingHandlers(NULL)
}, condition = identity)
## Error in globalCallingHandlers(NULL) : 
##  should not be called with handlers on the stack
```

```r
> packageVersion("pkgdown")
[1] '1.6.1'
```

title: suppress a section title from toc
description:
Pandoc >= 2.8 [supports](https://pandoc.org/MANUAL.html#heading-identifiers) excluding some heading by appending the `.unlisted` class, as in:

# My heading {.unlisted}
```

By extension, this also [seems to work](https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/issues/1625#issuecomment-558854773) in rmarkdown.
I confirmed that this works inside `rmarkdown::html_document()`.

However, pkgdown appears to ignore this setting, and headings inside articles marked as `.unlisted` are still included in the TOC.

For a rendered example, see https://subugoe.github.io/subugoetheme/articles/html_document.html.

I am guessing this does not work in pkgdown, because pkgdown uses it's own bootstrap TOC thingy, not vanilla pandoc (?).

title: Sync `clean_site()` with development mode
description:
When using auto development mode to maintain release and dev versions of the website, it can be a little tricky to ensure orphaned files are removed correctly. I _think_ this is already handled by `deploy_site_github()` via git commands, but it's difficult to achieve for other workflows (e.g. hosting on AWS S3).

I think it would be natural for `clean_site()` to support deleting files from the version of the website that is about to get rebuilt (i.e., either remove the `dev` folder or everything except the `dev` folder). That is, `clean_site()` could check the development mode and potentially the package version, before deciding which files to delete.

If you didn't want to change the default behavior, could we use an argument to trigger this behavior?

Then an AWS S3 workflow would look like:

1. `aws s3 sync s3://docs ./docs`
2. `pkgdown::clean_site()`
3. `pkgdown::build_site()`
4. `aws s3 sync ./docs s3://docs`

title: Add a trailing slash to enable Netlify redirects
description:
Hi @hadley,

We ran into trouble using [Netlify 200 rewrite redirects](https://docs.netlify.com/routing/redirects/redirect-options/) and pkgdown sites. To make it work, we needed to inject a teensy bit of JavaScript (written by @gadenbuie) into the pkgdown template. 

```
<script>
  if (!/(\/|html?)$/.test(window.location.href)){
    window.location.replace(window.location.href + '/');
  }
</script>
```

But, adding it inside `extra.js` won't help because it also won't be found due to the missing trailing slash problem. Here was @cderv's solution as a PR:

<https://github.com/apreshill/quillt/pull/3>

That is probably all you need to know, but I'll use the rest of this issue to "document" the play-by-play too, in case others run into the same trouble. Unfortunately, Netlify has no way to redirect the same url minus the trailing slash, so if you don't include the trailing slash in the url you see a site without CSS. The Netlify docs clearly state: 

> “You cannot use a redirect rule to add or remove a trailing slash.”

There is this related community discussion thread: <https://community.netlify.com/t/bug-in-non-trailing-slash-rewrite/452>

Explanation courtesy of @gadenbuie:

> The pkgdown site doesn't include the leading slash (i.e., `/quillt`, the package name we tested with) so when the page at `https://pkgs.rstudio.com/quillt` references `rmd.css,` the browser looks for it in the current path. This is normally the right thing to do, but here's where the redirect messes things up. Because the trailing slash isn't added, the browser thinks the current base path is `https://pkgs.rstudio.com/` without the `quillt`. So it looks for `https://pkgs.rstudio.com/rmd.css` instead of `https://pkgs.rstudio.com/quillt/rmd.css`.

template:

title: Packages attached via Depends are neglected
description:
{downlit} adds links for functions in attached packages. It populates the list of attached packages by searching for strings like `library()` and `require()`. However, it's possible for a package to attach other packages via the `Depends` field of its DESCRIPTION file. Could we please consider adding these dependencies as attached packages too?

As an example, consider the [{gganimate} README](https://gganimate.com). It features a code block:

```r
library(ggplot2)
library(gganimate)

ggplot(mtcars, aes(factor(cyl), mpg)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  # Here comes the gganimate code
  transition_states(
    gear,
    transition_length = 2,
    state_length = 1
  ) +
  enter_fade() +
  exit_shrink() +
  ease_aes('sine-in-out')
```

The {gganimate} package uses `Depends: ggplot2`, so calling `library(gganimate)` will automatically attach {ggplot2}. This issue is about making the `geom_boxplot()` link work without needing to call `library(ggplot2)` at the top.

title: Links to topics starting with period not working
description:
If a topic/function name starts with a period, the links to its page seem to be broken. In the following example
``` r
#' Example 1
#' 
#' @seealso [.f3()]
#' @family test
#' @export
.f1 <- function() NULL


#' Example 2
#' 
#' @family test
#' @export
.f2 <- function() NULL


#' Example 3
#' 
#' @export
.f3 <- function() NULL
```
the names of the generated help pages are e.g.
`/docs/reference/dot-f2.html`
but the hyperlinks in the see also-section of `.f1` point to 
`/docs/reference/.f2.html`,
resulting in an error when trying to follow the link. The hyperlinks on `/docs/reference/index.html` point to the correct addresses.

The html from the integrated R help server also points to the "wrong" adress, but this seems to be no issue, since the server automatically replaces the leading `.` with `dot-`.

As a workaround, manually specifying `@name dot-f1` seems to work, but this adds extra entries to the help index (and the redundant `@name` tags), so I'd rather avoid this.

pandoc's markdown_github does not respect user <div>
description:
I was having the same problem as #404 and I found that it is **due to a bug in pandoc's deprecated `markdown_github` when `--section-divs` are used**, which I illustrated [in this gist](https://gist.github.com/zkamvar/87e0730e55454156554c47283dd5ee37). In short, I **[found a solution](https://github.com/zkamvar/pkgdown/tree/znk-update-pandoc-markdown) and would like to submit a PR.** Read on for a few reprexes that illustrate the problem and solution. ## Problem With the current version of {pkgdown}, divs are collapsed: ``` r remotes::install_github("r-lib/pkgdown@eae56f0") library("pkgdown") library("usethis") library("xml2") tmp <- tempfile() create_package(path = tmp, check_name = FALSE, roxygen = FALSE, open = FALSE) cat("# Test", file = file.path(tmp, "README.md")) cat('# Test ### level 3
## level2
', file = file.path(tmp, "classy.md")) pkgdown::init_site(tmp) x <- read_html(file.path(tmp, "docs", "classy.html")) xml_find_all(x, ".//div[contains(@class, 'boo')]") #> {xml_nodeset (1)} #> [1]
\n
``` It's also worth noting that this engine does not appear to process the fenced divs either:
Unprocessed Fenced Divs ``` r remotes::install_github("r-lib/pkgdown@eae56f0") library("pkgdown") library("usethis") library("xml2") tmp <- tempfile() create_package(path = tmp, check_name = FALSE, roxygen = FALSE, open = FALSE) cat("# Test", file = file.path(tmp, "README.md")) cat('# Test ### level 3 ::: boo ## level2 ::: ', file = file.path(tmp, "classy.md")) pkgdown::init_site(tmp) x <- read_html(file.path(tmp, "docs", "classy.html")) xml_find_all(x, ".//div[contains(@class, 'boo')]") #> {xml_nodeset (0)} xml_text(x) # fenced divs unprocessed :'( #> [1] "Test • file79b649068d68\n \n \n \n \n \n Toggle navigation\n \n \n \n \n \n file79b649068d68\n 0.0.0.9000\n \n \n\n \n \n \n \n \n \n\n\n Reference\n\n \n \n\n\n \n\n \n \n \n Test\n \n\n\n\n\n\nlevel 3\n::: boo\n\n\n\nlevel2\n:::\n\n\n\n \n\n \n Contents\n \n\n\n\n\n\n \n Developed by First Last.\n\n\n\n Site built with pkgdown 1.5.1.9000.\n\n\n \n\n \n\n\n " ``` Created on 2020-08-18 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v0.3.0)
## Solution: use pandoc's `markdown` engine **I would like to submit a PR for this change if one of the maintainers agrees that it is cromulent.** I've created a fork of the repo and was able to fix this issue using `markdown` with the `markdown_github` options. There was initially the same issues that #1195 ran into, but i was able to fix them [using xpath manipulation](https://github.com/zkamvar/pkgdown/commit/1d2ece4c83de172c4e4e20dc83764273210f6e18#diff-909e6449ff4d4db377f6bfb40c34d7bb). The branch is here: https://github.com/zkamvar/pkgdown/tree/05175508ac8cef1b9d20755497bc1ce718aa2160 with a reprex: ``` r remotes::install_github("zkamvar/pkgdown@05175508") library("pkgdown") library("usethis") library("xml2") tmp <- tempfile() create_package(path = tmp, check_name = FALSE, roxygen = FALSE, open = FALSE) cat("# Test", file = file.path(tmp, "README.md")) cat('# Test ### level 3
## level2
', file = file.path(tmp, "classy.md")) pkgdown::init_site(tmp) pkgdown::build_home(tmp, preview = FALSE) x <- read_html(file.path(tmp, "docs", "classy.html")) xml_find_all(x, ".//div[contains(@class, 'boo')]") #> {xml_nodeset (1)} #> [1]
\n

\nCreated on 2020-08-18 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v0.3.0)
Fenced Divs are processed :) ``` r # remotes::install_github("r-lib/pkgdown@eae56f0") remotes::install_github("zkamvar/pkgdown@05175508") library("pkgdown") library("usethis") library("xml2") tmp <- tempfile() create_package(path = tmp, check_name = FALSE, roxygen = FALSE, open = FALSE) cat("# Test", file = file.path(tmp, "README.md")) cat('# Test ### level 3 ::: boo ## level2 ::: ', file = file.path(tmp, "classy.md")) pkgdown::init_site(tmp) pkgdown::build_home(tmp, preview = FALSE, quiet = TRUE) x <- read_html(file.path(tmp, "docs", "classy.html")) xml_find_all(x, ".//div[contains(@class, 'boo')]") # Fenced divs processed :) #> {xml_nodeset (1)} #> [1]

title: Q: Suggested workflow for NEWS.md rendering on package release?
description:
Hello,

I am using `development: mode: auto` for a dev and CRAN website.  The issue is that the call to https://crandb.r-pkg.org/googleAnalyticsR/all to determine the CRAN release date for the NEWS is not there until a few days after I've released, so now the [dev version has the date](https://code.markedmondson.me/googleAnalyticsR/dev/news/index.html) but the [CRAN version does not](https://code.markedmondson.me/googleAnalyticsR/news/index.html)

I tried rerunning the CD pipeline for the CRAN commit, but it didn't re-render the NEWs as its not changed.  

Should I add an explicit `build_news()` to the CI pipeline so it will build each push?  Will that avoid the caching?

The only option I see at the moment is to rollback the version, commit, then roll forward again which is a bit unoptimal.  Perhaps I should just wait until the CRAN update is live at the r-pkg.org link before incrementing to the dev version? 

I just wondered if you had tips on how you do it. :)

title: Incorrect highlighting of active navigation category
description:
There is a problem with the algorithm that determines which navbar item to highlight, introduced in #699 in an attempt to fix #660. If one uses the article index page to link to the articles, then when an article is opened, the "Get started" navbar item is highlighted instead of the "Articles" item. The following _pkgdown.yml illustrates this:
```
navbar:

  components:

      href: articles/index.html

articles:

```

title: Installing {magick} in Github Actions for macOS
description:
Github Actions kept failing for my [package](https://github.com/jhelvy/xaringanBuilder/actions) due to a dependency on the {magick} package. The error logs said `Configuration failed to find the Magick++ library`, so I needed to install `imagemagick` first _before_ installing the {magick} package dependency. 

After some trial and error, I found a fix by adding this to [my `pkgdown.yml`](https://github.com/jhelvy/xaringanBuilder/actions/runs/639234878/workflow) just before the `Install dependencies` step (I also needed `ffmpeg`):

```
      - name: Install magick dependencies
        run: |
          brew install imagemagick
          brew install ffmpeg
```

Just posting this here in case others have similar problems.

---
title: "example"

pkgdown:

---
```

title: Feature request: Allow for Horizontal  scrolling code blocks
description:
as pointed in #497 although the css was implemented in 03d93a1 but the R code that executes the examples doesn't allow for wide outputs. As it resets the console output width to 80 characters : https://github.com/r-lib/pkgdown/blob/6094ac3dd80a1f3f1d4e2f47d0ed4716d51362b0/R/build-reference.R#L177. When this line is changed to allow for wider outputs : ```r old_opt <- options(width = 10000) ``` The copy button gets misplaced when scrolling horizontally. ![](https://i.imgur.com/zvSETAt.png) I managed to circumvent this by changing the 83 line of the `pkgdown.js` file : https://github.com/r-lib/pkgdown/blob/6094ac3dd80a1f3f1d4e2f47d0ed4716d51362b0/inst/assets/pkgdown.js#L83 to : ```js $(".examples, div.sourceCode").wrap("
"); ``` basically wrapping the `pre` into `div` that'll be the parent to both the `button` and the `pre`.

title: Relative links on 404 page
description:
I have specified relative links in my `_pkgdown.yml`, for example:

```yml
navbar:
  components:
    get-started:
      text: Get started
      href: articles/Using-this-package.html
```
Where necessary 'pkgdown' seems to cleverly adapt these links by adding a `../` prefix, so that links do not become `.../articles/articles/...`. 

But this doesn't seem to be the case on the '404' page: [`https://me.github.io/my-package/articles/Nothing-here.html`](https://ms609.github.io/TreeDist/articles/Nothing-here.html) gives the helpful 404 message "use the links in the navbar", but these links contain an extra `articles` so do not themselves work.

One possible solution might be to use the entry in the `url:` yaml field to write the links on the 404 page?

title: The snippet `help(...)` inside a code tag breaks build_site()
description:
### Reprex ```r usethis::create_package(file.path(getwd(), 'down')) writeLines(r'-(#' Test #' #' Execute \code{help(a$b)} f = function () help(a$b))-', 'R/test.r') devtools::document() pkgdown::build_site() ``` ### Expected output A working package page is generated. ### Actual output Error message: ``` Reading 'man/f.Rd' Error in index[[topic]] : attempt to select more than one element in vectorIndex In addition: Warning messages: 1: In if (has_name(index, topic)) { : the condition has length > 1 and only the first element will be used 2: In if (has_name(index, topic)) { : the condition has length > 1 and only the first element will be used Error: callr subprocess failed: attempt to select more than one element in vectorIndex Type .Last.error.trace to see where the error occured ``` The same error message is also shown for slight variations of the ‘roxygen2’ comment above, for instance `\code{help(a-b)}`. title: pkgdown build/deploy action fails; can't find package mentioned in README but otherwise unused
description:
I have a data package, [covdata](https://github.com/kjhealy/covdata), that I build every few days. It passes R CMD check. Normally, its [website](https://kjhealy.github.io/covdata) is deployed to `gh-pages` by a pkgdown GitHub action. The action is identical to the `pkgdown.yaml` example in `r-lib/actions`. Today the action started to fail with the following error:

```
Error in find.package(package, lib.loc) :  there is no package called ‘drat’
Calls: <Anonymous> ... find_vignette_package -> <Anonymous> -> find.package
11 Removing worktree 11111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111
Running git worktree remove \
  /var/folders/24/8k48jl6d249_n_qfxwsl6xvm0000gn/T/RtmpMX9uKh/file74515d6f867
Execution halted
```

The [drat package](http://dirk.eddelbuettel.com/blog/code/drat/) is mentioned in the [README.Rmd](https://github.com/kjhealy/covdata/blob/6868321ec74f94da384c1338d832f05ae28e0509/README.Rmd) and [README.md](https://github.com/kjhealy/covdata/blob/6868321ec74f94da384c1338d832f05ae28e0509/README.md) files. It's mentioned as an option for installing the package with `install.packages()`, as an alternative to `install_github()`. However, `drat` is not part of the actual package in any way. The only place it is mentioned is in the README. In the course of trying to diagnose the problem, I also made sure that the mention in the `Rmd` file does not happen in a code chunk: it's just pure markdown. (Previously it had been in a code chunk with the `eval = FALSE` option set in the chunk header.)

So I'm not sure why this is happening. Why is pkgdown or GitHub action complaining it can't find this package?

title: get _pkgdown.yml url: from DESCRIPTION
description:
I understand that something like 

```yaml
url: https://subugoe.github.io/hoad/
```

in the `_pkgdown.yml` is necessary for proper cross-linking (and search?).

I'd imagine that this info is already included in the `DESCRIPTION` `URL` for many projects.

I'm on a bit of a quest to reduce duplication in code, and this is a small but somewhat confusing one.

Of course, as a complication, `DESCRIPTION` `URL` can include *many* URLs, not just the public-facing pkgdown one.
But I think it's a reasonable assumption that whichever of these `URL`s is *not* `github.com` or in any event, the same host as `BugReports`, *is* probably the public facing pkgdown site.

In my projects I now infer the `_pkgdown.yml` `url:` field like so:

```r
get_url_from_desc <- function() {
  all_urls <- desc::desc_get_urls()
  gh_urls <- sapply(all_urls, is_gh_url)
  public_urls <- all_urls[!gh_urls]
  public_urls[1]
} 

is_gh_url <- function(url) {
  httr::parse_url(url)$hostname == "github.com"
}
```

Would be happy to draft a PR to that effect.

title: pkgdown version 1.6 is not compatible with gif objects
description:
Hello all!

I recently updated `pkgdown` from version 1.5.1 to 1.6.1 and found that the update caused problems with vignette building. In particular, gif objects, in my case the result of `gganimate`, cause `pkgdown::build_site()` to error.

I have created a [small package](https://github.com/arisp99/PkgdownExample) on github to showcase this issue. When `pkgdown::build_site()` is run on `pkgdown` version 1.5.1, the article builds. However, when `pkgdown::build_site` is run on `pkgdown` version 1.6.1, an error message appears.

The vignette run and the error message can be found below.

``` r
library(PkgdownExample)
library(gganimate)
#> Loading required package: ggplot2

# Create a static ggplot
p <- ggplot(iris, aes(x = Petal.Width, y = Petal.Length)) +
  geom_point()

plot(p)
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/0TZRrKw.png)

``` r

# Animate the plot
p + transition_states(Species, transition_length = 2, state_length = 1)
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/vmjUARc.gif)

<sup>Created on 2020-09-12 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v0.3.0)</sup>

Error message:
```
-- RMarkdown error -------------------------------------------------------------
Quitting from lines 18-29 (Example.Rmd) 
Error : Unsupported device
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Error : Failed to render RMarkdown
Error: callr subprocess failed: Failed to render RMarkdown
Type .Last.error.trace to see where the error occured
```

Looking at the changelog of the `pkgdown` package, I suspect this error has something to do with the newly introduced usage of the `ragg` package. It does not seem that `ragg` has a function to draw to a gif file, but I may be misunderstanding the error message.

Any insight would be much appreciated!

title: Make 'eval.expr = TRUE' explicit in the call to 'yaml::yaml.load_file()'
description:
To read the `_pkgdown.yml` file, the function `yaml::yaml.load_file()` is called. This function has an argument `eval.expr` that currently defaults to `TRUE` (`yaml` version `2.2.1`). However, as per the function documentation: 

    There is a built-in handler that will evaluate expressions that are tagged with the ‘!expr’ tag. 
    Currently this handler is enabled by default, but the handler is being disabled by default in an 
    upcoming version for safety and security reasons. If you do not explicity set the eval.expr 
    argument to TRUE, you will get a warning if an expression is evaluated. 

Thus, for compatibility purposes, and in order to anticipate a next release of `yaml`, it would be desirable to set explicitly the argument `eval.expr` to `TRUE`.

title: Support radix / distill articles
description:
[radix](https://rstudio.github.io/radix/) is a new rmarkdown format for data scienc-y articles, based on Google's [distill](https://distill.pub) web framework.
Compared to the vanilla (slightly altered) `rmarkdown::html_document()` currently used within pkgdown, it has a couple of advantages:

- some layouting sugar (full-width figures, gutter footnotes, ...)
- extensive scholarly metadata support
- hoverable footnotes and citations

So I thought it'd be nice to support radix as an *article* format within pkgdown websites. 

I haven't thought through just how this might be accomplished, and there might be some stumbling blocks (conflicting css?).

If the maintainers might see some value in this, I'd be happy to research this further and give it a go if doable.

title: Provide an easy way to inject something in head.html?
description:
I know per https://github.com/r-lib/pkgdown/issues/1054 and https://github.com/r-lib/pkgdown/pull/984 that the current recommendation to cater for an alternative analytics provider is to create one's own template. 

I was wondering whether pkgdown could behave like bookdown (or like what some customizable Hugo themes do) where you can input the path to an HTML file to be injected at the end of head. 

In this way one could add something to add say Matomo analytics, or arbitrary meta tags, without needing to create and maintain a template.

Creating one's own template, that's just the standard pkgdown head + a few lines, works of course but it can get out-of-date fairly easily.

title: relative paths of external images in vignette "articles" are not built correctly if folder names contain spaces
description:
This is related to: https://github.com/r-lib/pkgdown/issues/1027

After cloning the repository for `rvest`, I figured out what might be explaining Thierry's problem, which I was also facing. 

It seems that when folder names have spaces (for instance `my folder`), then `build_site()` does build the html with the correct figure paths. 

To reproduce the problem, you can do the following:
- Clone `rvest`
- Include the `rvest` folder inside a folder with a space between names (for instance `my folder/rvest`)
- Run `pkgdown::build_site()`

Then you will see that the figures will not have the correct relative paths.

pkgdown: 1.5.1.9000
pkgdown_sha: ~
articles: []
last_built: 2020-07-22T05:05Z
urls:
  reference: https://pages.github.sydney.edu.au/speed-extract/mandrake//reference
  article: https://pages.github.sydney.edu.au/speed-extract/mandrake//articles
```

* `urls$reference` gives https://pages.github.sydney.edu.au/speed-extract/mandrake//reference
* `urls$article` gives https://pages.github.sydney.edu.au/speed-extract/mandrake//articles

pkgdown figures out the rest. 

## The problem with this process and enterprise hosted repos

This would be great, however, you will find that if you click on https://pages.github.sydney.edu.au/speed-extract/mandrake/pkgdown.yml

you will be given a challenge-response asking you to sign in.

curl says:

```
curl -I "https://pages.github.sydney.edu.au/speed-extract/mandrake/pkgdown.yml"
```

```
HTTP/1.1 302 Moved Temporarily
Server: GitHub.com
Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2020 06:27:49 GMT
Content-Type: text/html
Content-Length: 138
Location: https://github.sydney.edu.au/sessions/_auth_request_bounce?return_to=https%3A%2F%2Fpages.github.sydney.edu.au%2Fspeed-extract%2Fmandrake%2Fpkgdown.ym
```

So, `pkgdown` is never going to resolve those links. 

## Potential Fixes / Accomodations

I wonder, then, whether there are other ways pkgdown could accomodate linking enterprise hosted packages. 
A few jump out:

* __1__ Allowing `pkgdown.yml` (The one deployed wherever our pkgdown site is deployed, eg  https://pages.github.sydney.edu.au/speed-extract/mandrake/pkgdown.yml ) to be built into the package (Removing it from `.Rbuildignore` ) s.t if it is found, its url links are resolved automatically.
* __2__ If `pkgdown` attempts to resolve `DESCRIPTION$URL`/pkgdown.yml , and fails, pkgdown can make its best-effort based off of `DESCRIPTION$URL` to set up some "standard" links, such as:
  ```
  # base_url <- DESCRIPTION$URL
  urls$reference <- file.path(base_url, "reference")
  urls$article <- file.path(base_url, "articles")
  ```

These fall-backs might allow a best-effort linking for package's whose `description$url` field cannot be resolved publicly. I personally don't see too much harm in building a `pkgdown.yml` into installed R packages, so I think this could accomodate those of us who can't host all of our work publically. 

Cheers!

title: system-specific rdrr.io links are not resolved correctly
description:
When adding links to documentation on rdrr.io, pkgdown does not resolve system-specific links correctly.

In more detail: Some packages have system-specific Rd documentation files in `man/unix/*.Rd` and/or `man/windows/*.Rd` which are preserved with the `unix/` and `windows/` directories on rdrr.io. However, pkgdown currently does not include these directories when generating the links to rdrr.io.

Example: Including a link to `parallel::mclapply` links to
<https://rdrr.io/r/parallel/mclapply.html>
rather than
<https://rdrr.io/r/parallel/unix/mclapply.html>

Note: In Rd markup this is often coupled with `#ifdef` tags, see: <https://github.com/r-lib/pkgdown/issues/1384>

title: ifdef for linking to windows/unix-only man pages
description:
Sometimes you need to link to system-specific documentation (windows only or unix only) and the standard way of doing this in Rd is to use `#ifdef` constructs, see: <https://CRAN.R-project.org/doc/manuals/r-release/R-exts.html#Platform_002dspecific-sections>. However, this currently does not seem to work in `pkgdown`, leading to `Unknown tag: #ifdef/tag` messages and omission of the corresponding conditional documentation.

Is there some workardound for this or should this be declared differently for `pkgdown`?

Concrete example from one of our packages: For parallelization we use `parallel::mclapply()` except on Windows where it isn't available and we resort to `parallel::parLapply()`. Hence, the Rd text has:

```
... use either \code{\link[parallel:clusterApply]{parLapply}} (on Windows) or 
#ifdef windows
\code{\link[parallel:mcdummies]{mclapply}}
#endif
#ifdef unix
\code{\link[parallel]{mclapply}}
#endif 
(otherwise) ...
```

Depending on the system on which this package is installed, this will link to the _"mcdummies"_ help page (on Windows) or the _"mclapply"_ help page (otherwise). I'm not sure what would be the best general solution for `pkgdown`, e.g., always use the first element only or present both elements side by side with some markup?

Note also that on rdrr.io the corresponding help pages are in `unix/` and `windows/` subdirectories:
<https://rdrr.io/r/parallel/unix/mclapply.html>
<https://rdrr.io/r/parallel/windows/mcdummies.html>
