title: deploy_to_branch() fails on Windows using multiple git bash setup options, could be a processx::run() problem
description: Hi, Working with @lahuuki, we ran into a problem with `pkgdown::deploy_to_branch()` on Windows which I have now been able to reproduce on my Windows machine and well, that I'm very confused as to where the root of the issue is. It's very likely outside of `pkgdown`, but I'm reporting it here because `pkgdown::deploy_to_branch()` internally uses `processx::run()` to interact with `git`, while `usethis` relies on `git2r`, which does work on this Windows setup. Given that I'll likely have to report this issue elsewhere, all the code lives at https://gist.github.com/lcolladotor/f5575143cf07f46cdb9cabc6ebe8d5c9. ## Error description Running `pkgdown::deploy_to_branch()` on a brand new package eventually ends up running `pkgdown:::git("commit")` but this fails. It fails because `pkgdown` internally uses `processx::run("git")` and for some reason unknown to me, under this scenario, `git` does not find the `.gitconfig` file that specifies the username and email for the computer user. Thus the error can be reproduced with: ```R ## Create a package usethis::create_package("~/Desktop/testgit") ## Set up git and say yes to the prompts usethis::use_git() ## Create a file writeLines("hola", "test.txt") ## Use git2r to add it (can also be done with the RStudio git panel) git2r::add(path = "test.txt") ## Attempt to commit with the internal pkgdown code pkgdown:::git("commit", "-m", "hola") # Running git commit -m hola # # *** Please tell me who you are. # # Run # # git config --global user.email "you@example.com" # git config --global user.name "Your Name" # # to set your account's default identity. # Omit --global to set the identity only in this repository. # # fatal: unable to auto-detect email address (got 'fellg@DESKTOP-GB1AFPA.(none)') # Error in processx::run("git", c(...), echo_cmd = echo_cmd, echo = echo, : # System command 'git' failed, exit status: 128, stdout & stderr were printed # Type .Last.error.trace to see where the error occured ``` ## Related links * Investigating the output of `echo $PATH | tr ':' '\n'` from https://github.com/jennybc/happy-git-with-r/issues/67#issuecomment-341849422 * Git bash setup I had (and thus asked @lahuuki to copy): https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/2224#issuecomment-368260312 * I also tried both the default "use git from git bash only" (which doesn't work as reported at https://github.com/jennybc/happy-git-with-r/issues/67#issuecomment-343800308) and the middle option (now called) "Git from the command line and also from 3rd-party software" which does work in that same comment; see the "Reinstalling, the only option I change is" section of the comment. * No related issues (I think) at `pkgdown`: https://github.com/r-lib/pkgdown/issues?q=git+windows * Known Windows shell issues: https://happygitwithr.com/shell.html#windows-shell-hell. From https://github.com/jennybc/happy-git-with-r/issues?q=git+windows+config, https://github.com/jennybc/happy-git-with-r/issues/67 was the most related issue. ## Setup * R 4.0 * Rtools40 * RStudio version 1.2.5042 (latest stable release) * Install git bash https://git-scm.com/download/win. I have tested with all 3 options from In all three options, RStudio and `git2r::commit()` did work, while `processx::run("git")` failed. In the end, I have reverted back to my initial "Use git and optional Unix tools from the command prompt" option as recommended at https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/2224#issuecomment-368260312. ## Major confusions I still have no idea why `processx::run("git")` fails to find the user-contributed `.gitconfig` file under the different setups. Even the same `git` version (`/cmd/git` with `processx` https://gist.github.com/lcolladotor/f5575143cf07f46cdb9cabc6ebe8d5c9#file-debug_pkgdown-r-L89 and RStudio's terminal with git bash https://gist.github.com/lcolladotor/f5575143cf07f46cdb9cabc6ebe8d5c9#file-debug_pkgdown-r-L196) leads to different `git config --list --show-origin` outputs (`processx` one https://gist.github.com/lcolladotor/f5575143cf07f46cdb9cabc6ebe8d5c9#file-debug_pkgdown-r-L55-L85 vs https://gist.github.com/lcolladotor/f5575143cf07f46cdb9cabc6ebe8d5c9#file-debug_pkgdown-r-L199-L217) where `processx::run("git")` fails to find the `C:/Users/fellg/.gitconfig` file while RStudio's terminal with git bash does find it. Even using the "Use git from git bash only" git bash installation route, I can make git commits with `git2r` and RStudio git's panel. Using the same `git.exe` path that RStudio uses (inspired from https://github.com/r-lib/processx/issues/161), I however end up with the same `processx::run()` error (the function used internally by `pkgdown`). ## Moving forward * Maybe you have a better idea on how to find the root issue behind `pkgdown`/`processx::run("git")` on Windows (likely involves creating an issue at https://github.com/r-lib/processx/). * Maybe there are other Git for Windows setup options that you know of that we can try out (likely involves creating an issue at https://github.com/jennybc/happy-git-with-r/) * Maybe `pkgdown` could use `git2r` instead, like `usethis`. It seems to me that this would involve editing https://github.com/r-lib/pkgdown/blob/fcc120d996055519db89f37f0097af7ce25d6641/R/deploy-site.R#L222-L224 and the rest of the `pkgdown:::git()` calls in that script (I might be missing other ones). However, the git history for that file looks quite complicated and there's potentially other complications I'm unware of https://github.com/r-lib/pkgdown/commits/fcc120d996055519db89f37f0097af7ce25d6641?before=fcc120d996055519db89f37f0097af7ce25d6641+35&path%5B%5D=R&path%5B%5D=deploy-site.R. If you like this option, I could try to submit a PR for it. * One simpler option would be to rely on `git2r` for making the commits (or any other git step that requires having a username and email specified in the `.gitconfig`) and leave the rest unchanged (it would add `git2r` to the dependencies of `pkgdown`, which is maybe something you are trying to avoid doing). Thank you again for your help `r-lib`! Best, Leo

title: FR: Development mode "preview"
description:
as an extension of "auto".

- x.y.z version: to `docs/` 
- x.y.z.9000 version, main branch: to `docs/dev`
- x.y.z.9000 version, other branch: to `docs/preview/<branch-name>`

Similar to Netlify preview, without having to host at Netlify. Useful gimmicks:

- clean stale previews
- if branch has an associated pull request, post a comment with link to preview

Related: #1057.

title: `build_site()` fails when a Sexpr is in the Title
description:
This only happens in the development version of pkgdown, it works with the CRAN version.

I have used a `\Sexpr` line in the Title, like this:

```r
#' \Sexpr[stage=render,results=rd]{"hi"} Test
#'
#' @description
#' Hi there
#'
#' @export
test_fn <- function() {
  1
}
```

`build_site()` fails with:

```r
> pkgdown::build_site()
Error: Context `src_path` has not been initialised
```

A backtrace:

```r
> rlang::last_error()
<error/rlang_error>
Context `src_path` has not been initialised
Backtrace:
  1. pkgdown::build_site()
  2. pkgdown::as_pkgdown(pkg, override = override)
  4. pkgdown:::package_topics(pkg, package)
  5. purrr::map_chr(rd, extract_title)
  6. pkgdown:::.f(.x[[i]], ...)
  6. purrr::detect(., inherits, "tag_title")
 13. pkgdown:::flatten_text(., auto_link = FALSE)
 15. purrr::map_chr(x, as_html, ...)
 17. pkgdown:::as_html.tag_if(.x[[i]], ...)
 19. pkgdown:::as_html.tag(x[[2]])
 20. pkgdown:::flatten_text(x, ...)
 21. purrr::map_chr(x, as_html, ...)
 23. pkgdown:::as_html.tag_Sexpr(.x[[i]], ...)
 25. pkgdown:::context_get("src_path")
```

A reproducible test package where this occurs is here:
https://github.com/DavisVaughan/testpkgdowntitle/blob/master/R/test.R

It seems like this happens because `as_pkgdown()` calls `package_topics()` to build the topics. `package_topics()` tries to extract all the titles with `extract_title()`, which tries to convert each title to HTML with `as_html()`. When it hits this title, `as_html.tag_Sexpr()` is run, but the context variable `src_path` hasn't been initialized yet.

title: Code blocks consisting of commented lines only are not syntax highlighted
description:
A change in the way code blocks are highlighted at https://github.com/r-lib/pkgdown/commit/f49ffa50fb609b72e7fd09a334bbbc707404e7aa has lead to blocks consisting of `#` **only** no longer receiving the markup that leads to the syntax highlighting (whereas comment lines in mixed code/comment blocks do). This has lead to inconsistent highlighting in e.g., vignettes where some code chunks have separate output and input blocks. A minimal reprex: ```r package.skeleton("x") dir.create("x/vignettes") cat("```r\n#\n```", file = "x/vignettes/x.Rmd") pkgdown::build_article("x", "x") html <- xml2::read_html("x/docs/articles/x.html") src <- xml2::xml_find_first(html, ".//div[contains(@class, 'sourceCode')]") as.character(src) ``` Prior to https://github.com/r-lib/pkgdown/commit/f49ffa50fb609b72e7fd09a334bbbc707404e7aa produces: ``` [1] "
#
" ``` and since then the output is: ``` [1] "
#
" ``` which fails to trigger syntax highlighting. A solution is proposed with https://github.com/r-lib/pkgdown/pull/1310 by allowing `pkgdown:::highlight_text()` to add markup to some empty expressions. Note that this is a related to, but distinct from https://github.com/r-lib/pkgdown/issues/1296

At https://travis-ci.com/ComunidadBioInfo/regutools/builds/144932233 I do see that `TRAVIS_DEPLOY_KEY` is set but maybe I need to add some other environment variable on my `.travis.yml` file https://github.com/ComunidadBioInfo/regutools/blob/c4e30073e3e0aa0d75aa824c5904b4e1eb721360/.travis.yml. I looked at a few other `.travis.yml` files at `github.com/ropenscilabs` like `circle` and `travis` but they use other tools (`tci` as in `tic::deploy()` for https://github.com/ropenscilabs/circle/blob/master/.travis.yml) which feels like a new rabbit hole :P.

```
Setting environment variables from repository settings
$ export TRAVIS_DEPLOY_KEY=[secure]
```

If you have other ideas on what else I should try or how I can get more information for debugging this please let me know. Thank you!

Best,
Leo

title: Idea: `browse_package()`
description:
**EDIT: This was aimed to be an issue in usethis, not pkgdown. Can someone please transfer it? Thanks and sorry.** 😆 

I often find myself in the situation wanting to browse the pkgdown site of a package rather than its GitHub or CRAN site.

I am currently using `browseURL(desc::desc_get_urls()[1])` for this which opens the pkgdown site if it exists in the URL field and comes first. If missing, the GitHub page is opened. If no URL field exists, it errors obviously.

Some pkgs do not have a URL field at all and while `usethis::browse_github()` already falls back to `usethis::browse_cran()`, I have the feeling that a wrapper function like `browse_package()` could be helpful.

Essentially it would try to look for a pkgdown page first, fall back to the GitHub page and last to the CRAN page.

title: Use VignetteIndexEntry to build articles index
description:
Currently, the vignette `index.html` page (https://pkgdown.r-lib.org/articles/ or https://pkgdown.r-lib.org/articles/index.html) is a list with the titles of the vignettes.

Given that it's an index of the vignettes, it would make more sense to use `\VignetteIndexEntry` rather than `title` IMO. Plus, it would match the listing on CRAN.

title: UTF-8 Encoding in README
description:

You can see the rendered HTML from README.Rmd here: https://openplantpathology.github.io/Reproducibility_in_Plant_Pathology/

This happens locally using macOS and using the GitHub pkgdown actions from r-lib, https://github.com/openplantpathology/Reproducibility_in_Plant_Pathology/blob/master/.github/workflows/pkgdown.yml.

I've set the encoding to UTF-8 in DESCRIPTION, https://github.com/openplantpathology/Reproducibility_in_Plant_Pathology/blob/master/DESCRIPTION

I don't recall this having been an issue in the past, I just noticed it today.

title: v1.5.0: Breaking changes in sidebar
description:
Hi, I'm having some trouble updating my `extra.css` file to reflect breaking changes introduced in the latest pkgdown v1.5.0 update. For reference, here's my custom pkgdown CSS file shared across my packages: https://github.com/steinbaugh/steinbaugh.github.io/blob/master/css/pkgdown.css Note that `div#sidebar` has changed to `div#pkgdown-sidebar` in v1.5.0. In the previous version, the sidebar HTML was rendered as such: ```html

Contents

  • Arguments
  • Value
  • Details
  • Note
  • Examples
``` source: https://github.com/acidgenomics/syntactic/blob/v0.3.8/docs/reference/camelCase.html In the latest update, the structure of the sidebar has changed: ```html

Contents

``` source: https://github.com/acidgenomics/syntactic/blob/v0.3.9/docs/reference/camelCase.html I'm assuming the sidebar table of contents (TOC) list is now handled by some type of JavaScript code. The current output is a bit of a regression in my opinion, as the source code doesn't contain the navigation elements in the HTML anymore.

title: Vignette sections with NOT_CRAN are not evaluating in v1.5.0
description:
Hello, I have two vignettes for an API wrapper package that use NOT_CRAN extensively for documentation. I've used the convention established in packages like [googlesheets](https://github.com/jennybc/googlesheets/blob/master/vignettes/managing-auth-tokens.Rmd) to have examples render to markdown but not run in CRAN checks. 
`NOT_CRAN <- identical(tolower(Sys.getenv("NOT_CRAN")), "true")`

The vignettes are here: https://github.com/hrecht/censusapi/tree/master/vignettes

After updating to pkgdown 1.5.0 those sections are no longer displaying the code results when knit by pkgdown. When I use the knit button in RStudio they do evaluate properly. The code should get some data via API and then display the first rows using `head()`. I receive no error messages, but no data is shown in the resulting article pages. All of the text and code compile properly, it's just the code evaluation results that seem to be an issue.

I made one of the two vignettes online-only and removed any NOT_CRAN mentions and that seemed to fix the pkgdown compiling issue for that article. I've troubleshooted but am not totally sure what the issue is in my code. Are there some changes that need to be made in RMarkdown to make code run in pkgdown but not CRAN in the new version?

Thanks for such a great package!

title: Multi-level table of contents
description:
It seems to be a good idea to visually display the document's nested structure created with headers of different order (h1, h2, etc.). Maybe [this comment](https://github.com/r-lib/pkgdown/issues/817#issuecomment-438051320) was about this feature, but I decided to create a separate issue.
Current pkgdown version can include headers of different depth, but they all "blend" together, which makes it harder to visually see an article's structure.

I recently discovered a way to deal with this situation:

- Post-process created html pages with ToC by adding "toc-lev{x}" class to ToC elements, where "{x}" represents the level of entry (1 is the highest; second is nested into first; etc.). Solution is a little bit "hacky", which uses the way ToC is currently created for articles with nested sections:

<details><summary>Code for modification of one html file based on its path</summary>

```r
add_toc_levels <- function(path) {
  page <- xml2::read_html(path)

  toc_items <- page %>%
    # Find table of contents by id
    xml2::xml_find_first(xpath = "//*[@id='tocnav']") %>%
    # Find all <li> (list elements) with "linkable" descendants which are
    # assumed to represent TOC entries
    xml2::xml_find_all(xpath = "descendant::li[descendant::a[@href]]")

  # Compute levels of entries by counting number of ancestors with class "nav-stacked":
  # they represent headers, into which current entry is nested
  toc_level <- vapply(toc_items, function(item) {
    xml2::xml_find_all(
      item, xpath = "ancestor::*[contains(@class, 'nav-stacked')]"
    ) %>%
      length()
  }, numeric(1))

  toc_class <- paste0("toc-lev", toc_level)

  # Add appropriate classes
  lapply(seq_along(toc_items), function(i) {
    xml2::xml_set_attr(toc_items[i], attr = "class", value = toc_class[i])
  })

  xml2::write_html(page, path)
}
```
</details>

- Add CSS rules for those classes to visually separate different levels. For example, `padding-left: 20px;` for "toc-lev2", `padding-left: 40 px;` for "toc-lev3", etc. This will create "tabbed" structure.

If you think this solution can live in pkgdown, let me know and I'll gladly make a PR.

Error in yaml.load(readLines(con), error.label = error.label, ...): argument "error.label" is missing, with no default

title: Improve article index
description:
As the number of vignettes in a package grows (e.g. <https://dplyr.tidyverse.org/dev/articles/>), the articles drop down becomes a less attractive way of selecting articles. It also fails to provide any context for the articles, so unless the title is immediately descriptive, it's hard to tell which vignette is most likely to help.

The most natural way to resolve this problem was suggested by @jennybc — scrap the dropdown, and instead use the same tools to organise the articles page as the reference page. This would make it possible to control the order of articles, separate them into categories, and provide an additional text description.

title: Use repr_html for values in examples.
description:
The [repr](https://github.com/IRkernel/repr) package allows to format values in a nicer way than just by text.

It would be great if pkgdown would use `repr::repr_html` to render the output of example code in `replay_html.value`, instead of just text via `capture.output(print(x$value))`

title: Support custom printing in example rendering
description: Currently, the rendering of example code uses the standard `print` method for the output. It would be great to be able to have more complex output by providing a `pkgdown_print()` method in the same veins as `knit_print`, or alternatively use knitr to render the example section.

title: allow customization of navbar articles order
description:
For `pkgdown` websites with a number of vignettes that might be logically ordered / grouped.

One simple solution: allow the navigation bar to be customized from within the `articles:` section; e.g. (copying from https://pkgdown.r-lib.org/reference/build_site.html)

```
articles:
  navbar:
    text: Articles
    menu:
    - text: Category A
    - text: Title A1
      href: articles/a1.html
    - text: Title A2
      href: articles/a2.html
    - text: -------
    - text: "Category B"
    - text: Title B1
      href: articles/b1.html
```

This would use the same format as for explicitly-defined navbars, but allow users to customize only this specific navbar as desired (leaving the rest as pkgdown default).

It could also be worth allowing short-form specifications of the vignettes, where the text is inferred from the title of the vignette used in a particular location. E.g. something like:

```
articles:
  navbar:
    text: Articles
    menu:
    - vignette: introduction
    - section: Collaborating
    - vignette: collaborating-a
    - vignette: collaborating-b
```

The main advantage of this approach is that it allows `pkgdown` websites to adapt to changes in the default navbar layout / display, if they change as newer versions of `pkgdown` are released.

title: articles yml does not control articles section dropdown menu
description:
This issue is similar to #995 and #325 

This minimal example shows what appears to be a problem the yml for controlling the dropdown navigation for articles.

The yml below should do the following, but it does not: 1) rename the "articles" tab, 2) write a line of text in the article dropdown tab, and 3) re-order the listed articles to show Article2 before Article1. Additionally, deleting one of the articles from the list under menu does not eliminate it from the dropdown navigation.

```
navbar:
  components:
    articles:
      text: New Name for Articles not showing
      menu:
      - text: This Text doesn't show
      - text: Article2
        href: articles/Article2.html
      - text: Article1
        href: articles/Article1.html
```

link to minimal example:

[https://github.com/CrumpLab/pkgdownMenuProblem](https://github.com/CrumpLab/pkgdownMenuProblem)

Many apologies if this has already been solved. I've attempted to read all of the issues and documentation, and still can't get it to work, so started to wonder if there was a bug, thanks for all the great work on pkgdown!

title: Support other code hosts
description:
e.g. GitHub enterprise (#676), GitLab (#1045), and sub-directories (#1152)

This requires at least the ability to configure the following URLs:

* A home page, equivalent to (e.g.) `https://github.com/r-lib`, for the navbar.
* A source url, equivalent to (e.g.) `https://github.com/r-lib/pkgdown/blob/master/{path}`, for reference and article source links.
* An issue url, equivalent to (e.g.) `https://github.com/r-lib/issues/{number}`, for NEWS links.
* A person url, equivalent to (e.g.) `https://github.com/{username}`, for NEWS links.

description:

For example, 

```

  - title: "Foo"
    contents:
      - wrong_filename
```

on `pkgdown::build_site()` will yield:

```
In '_pkgdown.yml', topic must be a valid R expression.
Problem topic: `wrong_filename`
```

I think I understand that this makes technical sense, but it can be confusing for the user.
I initially set off on the wrong track, futzing around with `"` valid R object names etc.

I'll be happy to take a crack at this if you think this makes sense.

title: Pass `quiet` down to `pkgdown::build_home()`
description:
When building pkgdown docs on travis, it might be useful to let `verbose = TRUE` display the output you get from `build_home(quiet = FALSE)` as well. It seems like that would have helped debug [this](https://travis-ci.org/jimhester/vroom/builds/473081296#L3761) travis issue as the `quiet` argument is passed all the way down to the `callr::r_safe()` call that failed, see [here](https://github.com/r-lib/pkgdown/blob/923eea8c4379e200640a8c98578e82d335561478/R/rmarkdown.R#L30).

I think it would require the following changes:

- `build_site_local()` gets a `quiet` argument which is passed through to `build_home()`
- `build_site_external()` gets a `quiet` argument which is passed through to `build_site()`
- `build_site()` gets a `quiet` argument which is passed through to `build_site_local()` and `build_site_external()`
- `deploy_local()` gets a `quiet` argument which is passed through to `build_site()`
- `deploy_site_github()`'s `verbose` argument is passed through as `deploy_local(quiet = !verbose)`

Or maybe it would make sense for `deploy_site_github()` to also have a `quiet` argument, but that may be confusing.

title: testthat jekyll github pages deployment issue
description:
I already solved this but putting this out there in case. 

I am working on building a pkgdown website for my package: https://meghapsimatrix.github.io/simhelpers/index.html

When I was building site for my package and added tests using testthat, because testthat has the curly braces, my site didn't build. I found the solution here: 
https://github.community/t5/GitHub-Pages/GitHub-Pages-Builds-Fail/td-p/29172

I just had to add an empty file named .nojekyll in the root of my repository.

title: CNAME auto-generation can break CDN fronted sites
description:
The improved `build_cname()` functionality included with V1.2.0 causes me a bit of grief with my deployment architecture.

I have a GitHub hosted site (davidski.github.io/evaluator) that is fronted by AWS CloudFront at evaluator.severski.net. I need to put https://evaluator.severski.net into my `_pkgdown.yml` for links to be generated correctly for the canonical form of my site. With this in the URL field, pkgdown generates a CNAME which, if deployed, causes an infinite loop between my CDN and my origin site.

I'm able to work around this by putting the CNAME file into my .gitignore, but I wonder if there isn't a more elegant solution for this.

title: build_home(): reduced priority for "index.Rmd" in pkgdown v1.4
description:
While in [pkgdown v1.3](https://github.com/r-lib/pkgdown/releases/tag/v1.3.0) the priority for building the home **index.html** was as follows: 
https://github.com/r-lib/pkgdown/blob/42971af1df065ab4e804ce3ee741192468c8bbd4/R/build-home-index.R#L9

It was changed with [pkgdown v1.4](https://github.com/r-lib/pkgdown/releases/tag/v1.4.0)  to: 
https://github.com/r-lib/pkgdown/blob/383c7eebf71667bd0265248caec618606e99454f/R/build-home-index.R#L8

In order to be backward compatible, it would be great if the priority could be changed back to the one used in pkgdown v1.3 or as follows:

`c("index.md", "index.Rmd", "README.md",  "README.Rmd") `


This would be really helpful as our > 40 company open-source R package repositories (https://kwb-r.github.io/status), which all use **pkgdown**, rely on the fact that **index.Rmd** is prioritised higher than **README.md**

title: Markdown content in <details></details> no longer parsed
description:
We've been using the [`
`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/details) syntax to collapse more specific installation instructions in the README of our package: ```md
Installing Docker 1. Go to [Docker Desktop](https://www.docker.com/products/docker-desktop). 2. Download Docker for Windows or Mac (free login required) and follow the installation instructions. Note that Docker for Windows requires Microsoft Windows 10 Professional or Enterprise 64-bit: installing Docker _Toolbox_ for previous Windows versions will not work. 3. Open the Docker application. The Docker (whale) icon will appear in your menu or task bar and indicate if it is running correctly. 4. Make local drive(s) available for Docker containers: * On Windows: right click the Docker icon > `Settings` > `Shared drives` > Select the drive(s) where you will be processing radar files > Click `Apply`. * On Mac: click the Docker icon > `Preferences` > `File sharing` > Add the drive(s) where you will be processing radar files > Click `Apply & Restart`. 5. In R do `check_docker()`. 6. You can now use the bioRad functionality that requires Docker.
``` Which in pkgdown 1.3.0 rendered nicely as: In pkgdown 1.4.1 the Markdown in the `
` section is no longer parsed however: I assume the content is now just parsed as regular HTML. But it was a nice feature that Markdown was parsed in `

title: Figures in examples are always rendered on a white background
description:
It appears that all figures rendered as part of the example sections in the docs are with a fixed white background. This means that you can't control background colour/transparency through the `figures:` yaml setting.

Digging into it, the `recordedplot` returned by `as_data()` already has a white background, so any device setting will get drawn over. I have been unable to figure out why this is happening (you can make transparent background in knitr, so it doesn't appear to be a limitation in the evaluate package).

This would be really nice to have for pages that uses a non-white background theme e.g. https://ambient.data-imaginist.com (compare the from page figures with the references)

title: preserve formatting of package version in DESCRIPTION
description: E.g. `renv` currently has, in its DESCRIPTION file: ``` Version: 0.8.2-3 ``` However, the pkgdown website shows in the top-left corner: Note that the `-` has been transformed to a `.`. It would be nice if `pkgdown` could preserve the original formatting.

title: Add affiliations option to authors
description:
It would be great to have an option to include the affiliation of any package author and contributor. The `DESCRIPTION` file cannot contain this information, but a website can of course be more comprehensive in a lot of ways.

I would suggest to just add this to the already available `authors` field in `_pkgdown.yml`:

```yml
authors:
  Jane Doe:
    affiliation: "Faculty of Statistics and Tidyverse, Example University of Someplace, Someplace, Somewhere"
  John Doe:
    affiliation: "Faculty of R Cookbooks, Some University, Someplace, Somewhere"
```

This information could then be parsed for the `./authors.html` file.

For some package, [like ours](https://msberends.gitlab.io/AMR/index.html), it would be great if it could include doctoral titles or any other name prefix/suffix as well, as some packages are meant for academic research and this could be required by some university policies.

```yml
authors:
  Jane Doe:
    prefix: "Dr"
  John Doe:
    prefix: "Prof."
```

### Example how it is now:

Jane Doe. Author, maintainer.

John Doe. Author.

### Example with new affiliation:

**Jane Doe.** Author, maintainer. Faculty of Statistics and Tidyverse, Example University of Someplace, Someplace, Somewhere.

**John Doe.** Author. Faculty of R Cookbooks, Some University, Someplace, Somewhere.

### Example with new prefix:

Dr Jane Doe. Author, maintainer.

Prof. John Doe. Author.

### Example how this could be really awesome:

Dr Jane Doe<sup>1</sup>

Dr Jessa J. Doe<sup>1</sup>

Joanna J. Doe<sup>1</sup>

Prof. John Doe<sup>2</sup>

<sup>1</sup> Faculty of Statistics and Tidyverse, Example University of Someplace, Someplace, Somewhere.

<sup>2</sup> Faculty of R Cookbooks, Some University, Someplace, Somewhere.

title: help() should redirect to pkgdown documentation if reference is available, not to rdrr.io
description:
In my NEWS.md file from https://styler.r-lib.org/dev/news/index.html, I have this

> [...] See `help("caching")` for details. [...]

I can't / don't want to use `caching()` because it's a topic ([source](https://github.com/r-lib/styler/blob/master/R/ui-caching.R#L24-L36)), not a function you can all from the package. Also, I like `help()` (potentially with the pkg argument) because it a valid R command and will work when reading `README.md` or `NEWS.md` from R. 

When clicking on the highlighted `help("caching")`, I am directed to https://rdrr.io/r/utils/help.html (online documentation for `help`), not the pkgdown help site for caching (e.g. https://styler.r-lib.org/dev/reference/caching.html).
I assume that pkgdown falls back to rdrr.io for any function that is not defined in the package, also `help(<function name >)` but in that case, it would be nice to just redirect to the https://styler.r-lib.org/dev/reference/caching.html. Can we make it behave the same as `?<function name >`? This already works well with pkgdown (at least in [`NEWS.md`](https://styler.r-lib.org/dev/news/index.html#styler-1-1-1) of styler it seems).

***
Here is the screenshot from the news html page:

![Screenshot 2020-01-19 at 15 10 31](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/10477073/72682501-d7b6a780-3acd-11ea-86f9-047121636b49.png)

title: If package resides in repo sub-directory, source link is not correct
description:

In case the package resides in the sub-directory of a github repository, then linking of source files is not correct. 

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/4161918/65393473-3e76bf00-dd81-11e9-9ead-516c97ac1ed7.png)

It would be a nice option to have the sticker to the top of the sidebar, so the sticker can still be viewed while scrolling the main div of the home page.

this can be done by adding an a url path to point to the sticker in the _pkgdown.yml.

This is the screenshot of the new placement.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1755487/48385741-af5b3e00-e6bd-11e8-9cc0-463acf2477b3.png)

title: factor out deploy_local to bash script for GitHub actions
description:
The git work done by `deploy_local()`, `github_clone()` and `github_push()` has some overlap with the bash script in the language-agnostic [GitHub action for GitHub Pages](https://github.com/maxheld83/ghpages).

(The action and bash script still needs quite some improvement but is used by all sorts of projects, not just R).

If there's some interest, I'd be happy to look into this, perhaps this is something that can be factored out of pkgdown.

It should still be able to run locally, and it should be possible to take on the bash script/function *without* taking on the entire ghactions package as a dependency.

title: "cph" role on front page
description: For some of my packages the `cph` role is my organization, but they aren't `fnd` as projects are grant-funded.  I'd like the `cph` author role to appear on the front page.  I believe the roles appearing on the front page are currently hard-coded as `aut`, `cre`, and `fnd`.  It would be great if this could be configured somehow, such as a flag in the for the author in the `authors:` YAML field of `front_page: TRUE`.

title: Default pkgdown theme contrast
description:
Disclaimer: I was told about contrast yesterday, so I know very little.

On http://wave.webaim.org/report#/https://pkgdown.r-lib.org/index.html (click on contrast) it seems that contrast is too low 

* in the navbar

* for comments in code chunks.

Should a darker shade be used in these places?

Related to #782

title: Document and export deploy_local()
description:
The `deploy_site_github` function is configured to be specific to running on travis environment.  IMO it is nice to also have option to deploy to gh-pages branch locally instead of only on travis (and having the clone to temp directory & build there & push all automated in a function is much smoother than trying to do those steps manually).  

I wrote a little modification of the function to enable such local deployment: [gist](https://gist.github.com/AliciaSchep/f4287a4797d15d2b7923f12d5d9cc93d).  It enables you to preview the site, and then choose to push to gh-pages.  

Wondering if y'all might consider adding such functionality to `pkgdown`, either enabling the package's `deploy_site_github` function to also run locally or adding another function specific to local use?

title: Print stderr output from pandoc subprocess in build_site()
description:
When `pandoc` fails to render markdown it prints the problems to `stderr`. This gets captured by callr, however it is not used so `build_site()` fails like [this example](https://travis-ci.org/thomasp85/lime/jobs/592943941). 

```
── Building articles ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Writing 'articles/index.html'
Reading 'vignettes/Understanding_lime.Rmd'
Error : callr subprocess failed: pandoc document conversion failed with error 99
Error: callr subprocess failed: callr subprocess failed: pandoc document conversion failed with error 99
Execution halted
Script failed with status 1
```



Because pkgdown usually runs in CI and the problem may be specific to the version of pandoc on the server, this is difficult to debug. 

It would be helpful if `build_site()` would print stderr output from the pandoc process so the user can see pandoc warnings/errors that may cause the rendering to fail.

title: Combining external images with vignettes to make pkgdown article
description:
There is a similar, closed issue here: https://github.com/r-lib/pkgdown/issues/1027 which I feel is incomplete.

I have a package with a `vignettes` folder. Inside that folder is another folder called `images`. In the .Rmd I use `knitr::include_graphics(<full path to image file>)` in an Rmd chunk to display the image.
When I knit the vignette, the images render. However, if I use pkgdown the resulting article does not render the images.

I believe this is because the `docs` directory created by pkgdown needs to copy the images from `vignettes/images/`. I can see that the article's .html source file is trying to reference an image located in `images/<my_image.jpg>`, but there is no such directory called `images` inside `docs`. How can I trigger pkgdown to do a copy based on `<full path to image files>` ?

title: Travis/pkgdown sometimes fails when building the vignette due to memory, but not with the same objects earlier in R CMD check
description:
Hi,

I'm a bit puzzled with a particular repository that sometimes fails deploying from Travis to GitHub due to out of memory errors and sometimes doesn't . The memory error always happens when `pkgdown` is building the vignette. The closest `pkgdown` issue I could find was https://github.com/r-lib/pkgdown/issues/783 though that one was closed due to a lack of access to the code.


This particular package uses about 2.5 GB of RAM in memory of R objects simply to get going, so yes, it's a beast. Something that really puzzles me is that the examples run fine (`R CMD check`) and the Travis build never fails at that point. My understanding is that `pkgdown::deploy_site_github()` is run on a new R process at the end, such that it should in theory have the exact same memory to use as the R process that `R CMD check` earlier. However if the two R processes are active at the same time, this could double the memory and bring it close to the 7.5 GB RAM limit of the Google Compute Engine used by Travis as detailed [in their docs](https://docs.travis-ci.com/user/reference/overview/) leading to the cases where sometimes it runs out of memory and sometimes it doesn't.

I'd appreciate if you have any suggestions that I could try or if there's more information that I provide you.

Best,
Leo




## Hm... 

As I write this, I realize that a more likely case is that the R process running `pkgdown::deploy_site_github()` keeps all the same objects used in the examples around as when building the vignette. Currently my examples use code like this (includes roxygen format):

```R
#' ## Obtain the necessary data
#' if (!exists('ori_sce')) ori_sce <- fetch_data('sce')

## That object uses 2.08 of RAM as determined by pryr::object_size()
```

but then in the vignette I use `sce <- fetch_data('sce')`. Hm... However, I actually don't use that big object in the vignette. I created a fake version that I use then (96.5 Mb) ([details here](https://github.com/LieberInstitute/spatialLIBD/commit/e529d217844794bfbe3073a7a79184838a1704bf)). 

I will test a version where I use the `if (!exists())` syntax with the same object names through both the docs and the vignette.

## Repository in question

* Package documentation website: http://research.libd.org/spatialLIBD/
* GitHub repository for the package https://github.com/LieberInstitute/spatialLIBD
* Travis build reports: https://travis-ci.com/LieberInstitute/spatialLIBD
* `.travis.yml` code that calls `pkgdown`: https://github.com/LieberInstitute/spatialLIBD/blob/2030888d0b0ef98fc4409d749af1b5f62dec8ae0/.travis.yml#L10-L13
* Note that you will need `RcppAnnoy` version 0.0.14 instead of the latest (from today) version 0.0.15  (due to [this issue](https://github.com/LTLA/BiocNeighbors/issues/10)) which you can install with `remotes::install_version('RcppAnnoy', version = '0.0.14')` as done in the `.travis.yml` code [here](https://github.com/LieberInstitute/spatialLIBD/blob/2030888d0b0ef98fc4409d749af1b5f62dec8ae0/.travis.yml#L15-L17). 

Unlike when I wrote https://twitter.com/fellgernon/status/1231483308120444929?s=20, I can now actually post an issue since we made the GitHub repository public [so we could submit it to Bioconductor](https://github.com/Bioconductor/Contributions/issues/1389).


## Locally

Unlike the previous issue https://github.com/r-lib/pkgdown/issues/783, I do not encounter this problem locally on my macOS (16 GB of RAM). I even made a script that I would run manually to update my website using the internals of `pkgdown`. While monitoring the memory usage with the macOS Activity Monitor, I saw no jumps during this whole process, also unlike https://github.com/r-lib/pkgdown/issues/783.

```bash
$ more update_spatialLIBD.sh
#!/bin/bash

# sh ~/Dropbox/code/update_spatialLIBD.sh

cd ~/Dropbox/Code/spatialLIBD
## Note the upgrade = FALSE, otherwise I run into the already mentioned RcppAnnoy issue
## when deploying spatialLIBD to shinyapps.io
Rscript -e "remotes::install_github('LieberInstitute/spatialLIBD', upgrade = FALSE); pkgdown:::deploy_local('.', repo_slug = 'LieberInstitute/spatialLIBD', commit_message = pkgdown:::construct_commit_message('.'))"
cd -
```

title: custom css for vignettes
description:
Hi! I have noticed that `pkgdown` somehow doesn't recognize any `css` that we might define in a specific vignette.

For example:

```yml
---
title: "Intro'"
output: 
  rmarkdown::html_vignette:
    css: style.css
vignette: >
  %\VignetteIndexEntry{Intro}
  %\VignetteEngine{knitr::rmarkdown}
  %\VignetteEncoding{UTF-8}
---
```

When I try to knit it myself to preview the output it works, but when I `pkgdown::build_site()` the `css` doesn't get recognized.

Anything I might be missing?

title: strange behaviour of \eqn
description:
Hi, I have seen something unexpected.
In the R help (Rd) `\eqn{\mum}` is seen correctly as μm, while in pkgdown (reference) gives error "\mum" (in red)
In contrast  `\eqn{\mu m}`  is seen separated (μ m) in R help (not wanted), while not-separeted in pkgdown: μm.

title: development version removed sidebar TOC highlighting
description:
I'm not sure if this is intended, but the current development version of `pkgdown` here on GitHub removed the automatic sidebar TOC highlighting as you scroll down a post.

I noticed that when reproducing the issue of https://github.com/r-lib/pkgdown/issues/1218 . To reproduce this, you can just clone Rvest and build the site using the default theme with the development version. Then remove the package, reinstall from CRAN, and build the site again.

title: Should pkgdown have a delete_site() function?
description: `pkgdown` automatically adds a lot of files to a user's repository.  Many users may not be quite sure what files are created by `pkgdown` (as opposed to, say, created by the many other similar helper functions in the`r-lib` / `devtools` universe).  I am a huge fan of these functions, but I also think it would be consistent with that same motivation of automating the creation from the R command-line if we could also automate the clean-up.  e.g. it would be great if there was a function like `delete_site()` (or maybe `remove_site()` that would reverse the effects of `build_site()`, that could remove components added by pkgdown.  Or perhaps there is a good reason not to do this? Or maybe deleting is too fraught with risk of removing something that wasn't auto-magically created?

title: pkgdown v1.4.0 adds href requirement for navbar
description:
in builds using v1.3.0, the `_pkgdown.yml` did not require the user to explicitly state `href` values for standard top-level menu components (like "reference") or explicitly state any sub components (such as specific vignettes) 

in builds with v1.4.0, the `_pkgdown.yml` file now requires the user to explicitly state `href` values and detail subcomponents, otherwise the content is rendered as text with a different formatting and no hyperlink.

a testing directory [here](https://github.com/dapperstats/test) has a working simple example. the most recent commit has a version that works under 1.3.0 but not under 1.4.0, as is evident from the [deployed site](https://dapperstats.github.io/test/) (built via travis).

i can reproduce this locally using `pkgdown::build_site()`:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/23511502/64573891-e45a1080-d321-11e9-9b2a-be20c2a0410c.png)
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/23511502/64573895-e623d400-d321-11e9-97a1-b3d622bca1c3.png)
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/23511502/64573899-e9b75b00-d321-11e9-82da-6fa1a62e4f78.png)
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/23511502/64573900-ecb24b80-d321-11e9-9b78-bedafd6df78a.png)

the code that works with 1.3.0 but not 1.4.0:
```
url: https://dapperstats.github.io/test
development:
  mode: auto
navbar:
  structure:
    left: [home, reference]
  components:
    reference:
      text: "Functions"
```

to make it work under 1.4.0, all that was needed was to explicitly state the `href`
```
url: https://dapperstats.github.io/test
development:
  mode: auto
navbar:
  structure:
    left: [home, reference]
  components:
    reference:
      text: "Functions"
      href: reference/index.html
```

this behavior was observed in the wild first while working on the [portalcasting](https://github.com/weecology/portalcasting) package.
it manifested in a few additional ways that aren't reproduced explicitly in this toy example, but might be caused by the same underlying component(?):
1. it dropped the github icon link that was previously just mentioned in the `structure` component, because the github component wasn't explicitly called out.
2. it dropped the vignette menu because the menu wasn't explicitly built out.

[the version of the yml that worked on 1.3.0](https://github.com/weecology/portalcasting/blob/ac0774fb79a8bc3713c547a0cc4367e658cc6518/_pkgdown.yml)
[what it needed to be changed to to work on 1.4.0](https://github.com/weecology/portalcasting/blob/master/_pkgdown.yml)

title: Implement bookdown like cross references
description:
I currently use **bookdown** for writing vignettes by adding the following to the YAML metadata:

```
output:
  bookdown::html_document2:
    base_format: rmarkdown::html_vignette
    number_sections: false
```

This allows me to reference equations and figures using the `\@ref(eq:some-equation)` syntax, and the vignettes render as you would expect. However, when using `pkgdown::build_articles()`, the cross references are no longer supported, and thus don't display correctly. It would be nice if **pkgdown** were also able to use the cross references feature.

title: Suggestion: Use more sensible default value for pkgdown.internet
description:
https://github.com/r-lib/pkgdown/blob/b7ca56bf8a40fc9166b3f44b50b85b341c3d1cdb/R/utils.r#L117

The default for `pkgdown.internet` is `TRUE` meaning you always need to set `options(pkgdown.internet = FALSE)` if you're offline and remember to turn it back on when you go back online.

Since `pkgdown` needs `curl` anyway I suggest setting the default value to `curl::has_internet()`. That way, `pkgdown` will use an available internet connection by default but not error out if there is no internet connection.

The required change would be minimal (change the line to `getOption("pkgdown.internet", default = curl::has_internet())`). I will gladly submit a PR if that is necessary.

title: unused argument (recurse = TRUE) error when building site
description:
Hi,

I just updated pkgdown to 1.4.0 and got this error from `build_site()`:
```r
> pkgdown::build_site()
Error in grep(x = path, pattern = regexp, value = TRUE, invert = isTRUE(invert),  : 
  unused argument (recurse = TRUE)
```

The traceback showed that it came from `fs::dir_ls()` not having a `recurse` argument:
```r
> traceback()
6: path_filter(files, glob, regexp, invert = invert, ...)
5: dir_ls(base, regexp = "\\.[rR]md$", recurse = TRUE)
4: package_vignettes(pkg)
3: structure(list(package = package, version = version, src_path = path_abs(pkg), 
       dst_path = path_abs(dst_path), github_url = pkg_github_url(desc), 
       desc = desc, meta = meta, figures = meta_figures(meta), development = development, 
       topics = package_topics(pkg, package), tutorials = package_tutorials(pkg, 
           meta), vignettes = package_vignettes(pkg), topic_index = topic_index_local(package, 
           pkg), article_index = article_index_local(package, pkg)), 
       class = "pkgdown")
2: as_pkgdown(pkg, override = override)
1: pkgdown::build_site()
```

So I updated my `fs` from 1.2.7 to the latest on CRAN (1.3.1), and now the error's gone.
```r
> packageVersion("fs")
[1] ‘1.2.7’

# Updated to fs 1.3.1 - it works now!
> install.packages("fs")
> pkgdown::build_site()
```

---

It looks like fs added the `recurse` argument in [1.3.0](https://github.com/r-lib/fs/blob/master/NEWS.md#fs-130), but pkgdown still depends on fs (>= 1.2.0). Should this be bumped to fs (>= 1.3.0)?

description:

```r
find_logo <- function(path) {
  path_first_existing(

    path(path, "man", "figures", "logo.svg"),
    path(path, "logo.png"),

title: Error : Unknown type: character when building site
description:
When I build my package docs (`surveydata`), I get  this error message:

```
Error : Unknown type: character
```

This happens because I have this code in my package:

`<edit>`

```
#' Updates names and variable.labels attribute of surveydata.
#'
#' @usage "names(x) <- value"
#' @param x surveydata object
#' @param value New names
#' @export
#' @seealso [surveydata-package()], [is.surveydata()]
`names<-.surveydata` <- function(x, value) {
  xattr <- attributes(x)
  ret <- as.data.frame(x)
  names(ret) <- value
  names(attr(ret, "variable.labels")) <- value
  as.surveydata(ret, ptn = pattern(x))
}
```

`</edit>`

The root cause is that `usage_type()` in `usage.R` checks for various object types, but throws an error when the parsed object is of type `character`.

I have a fix for this and will submit a PR imminently.

title: navbar: by default use 'Functions', not 'Reference'?
description:
Just started to explore it, and I find `pkgdown` a great package, thanks for providing such nice functionality!

This is a request to make the `navbar` labels more understandable to the average R-user / website visitor. Especially, _the meaning of '**Reference**'_ is not that intuitive to visitors of a website.

Myself and as it appears, others as well ([example](https://ropensci.github.io/git2rdata/) of @ThierryO ), are inclined to override `pkgdown`'s default by replacing:

- 'Reference' by '**Functions**'
- 'Articles' by '**Tutorials**'

But, such customization has the disadvantage of missing out new features & improvements that `pkgdown` can add in the future! (which is a reason for @peterdesmet to make an [issue](https://github.com/inbo/watina/issues/15) of pkgdown site customization)

So, that is why we would like to see these default navbar labels changed in the `pkgdown` package. Thanks for taking into consideration!

title: `mode: auto`  is ignored when using `deploy_site_github()`
description:
Using `build_site()` and `mode: auto` in `_pkgdown.yml` allow to have an 'danger' label for development version.
But, when using `deploy_site_github()` and Travis CI, the parameter is just ignored, allowing the website to be published with x.x.x.9000 version as a "release" version.

It would be great, to have `mode: auto` working with `deploy_site_github()`.

I don't know (yet) how the version is parsed inside pkgdown, but [deploy-site.R#L123](https://github.com/r-lib/pkgdown/blob/master/R/deploy-site.R#L123) seems to be a start to allow `mode:  auto` with `deploy_site_github()` and Travis CI.
If I manage to understand the version parser and deploy thing, I'll make a PR.

description:

#' 
#' bar
#' ```

foo

```

title: Error if documenting S4 method for class NULL
description:
I have an S4 method that I want to return `NULL` if the argument is `NULL`.

```
projection.NULL <- function(x,asText=TRUE) { return(NULL) }
setMethod('projection', signature(x='NULL'), projection.NULL)
```

The method seems to work as intended. `R check --as-cran` mandates that I document this function, which I do as 

```
\S4method{projection}{NULL}(x,asText=TRUE)
```

This all seems to work fine for rendering and passing `R check --as-cran`, but then any `pkgdown` function crashes, such as

```
> library(ctmm)
> pkgdown::build_news()
Error: Result 1 must be a single string, not a character vector of length 0
Call `rlang::last_error()` to see a backtrace
```

We have tracked this down to `purrr::map_chr(as.list(x[[3]][-1]), as.character)`, which doesn't like `NULL` (https://github.com/ctmm-initiative/ctmm/issues/29#issuecomment-468299470)

If I've done something non-kosher with S4 methods, I apologize for wasting your time. I'm not very familiar with S4 and am importing this method from another package.

title: Help add privacy policy when Google Analytics is being used
description:
I love that `pkgdown` makes it easy to add Google Analytics to the website. This seems like it could provide useful insights to package developers into what users are finding interesting or useful.

One "gotcha" of using Google Analytics is that it puts the onus on users to create a privacy policy. However, many package developers may not realize this or have access to legal resources to consult on complete and correct language to include. 

Would there be a benefit to making `pkgdown` more opinionated about this? Some options might include:

- Including in the docs where Google Analytics is mentioned a call-out about a Privacy Policy being needed and instructions on how to add one
- Taking an opinionated approach of providing a message/warning or throwing an error if the `ganalytics` parameter is being used without a `PRIVACY.md` file existing
- Ideally, consulting with RStudio legal resources to determine a boiler plate text for said policy (obvious this would be a YMMV). This could live somewhere in either `pkgdown` or perhaps `usethis` could even take on a `use_privacy_policy()` function.

The third option could also be useful for `blogdown` which has the same issue.

I'd be interested in helping out if any of these options seems desirable! 🙋 Thank you so much for this amazing package!

---

FWIW: For my [`pkgdown` site for `projmgr`](https://emilyriederer.github.io/projmgr/), I added a policy by adding a `PRIVACY.md` file to my repo and adding the following to my `_pkgdown.yml`:

```
home:
  links:
  - text: "Site Privacy Policy"
    href: PRIVACY.html
```

For the text, I borrowed the same verbiage I found on the [US House of Representatives](https://www.house.gov/privacy-policy) website regarding Google Analytics since I do not have a legal background to write the language myself.

description:

Many packages seem to have pre-rendered example code in the `readme.md` that doesn’t work out of the box. It would be useful to support a `_pkgdown.yml` option which lets the author opt-out of knitting the `readme.md`, i.e. convert it to index.html as is.

I had actually expected that the code would only be knit if it was an `Rmd` file and not for `md` files. One could also consider making this the default behavior.

description:

- only open each target once
- only open links from the main text, not from the menu
- alert if more than n tabs are about to be opened.

I'm aware there are browser extensions that do this, but our implementation could provide better value here.

title: Parameterize a package template?
description:
When the template of a pkgdown website is a _package_, what happens is that the assets are copied.

https://github.com/r-lib/pkgdown/blob/0b2c27d41b869ac31b6a46815940f55b12f6171f/R/init.R#L70-L72

I wonder whether this step could be made more complex to be able to parameterize the template. I'd like to be able to e.g. add a warning banner to the website based on the development status, i.e. the config could look like

```yaml
template:
  package: rotemplate
  status: concept
```

and based on this the assets from `rotemplate` would be rendered like what happens in `usethis` with `whisker`.

https://github.com/r-lib/usethis/blob/a330ed9c39fd4d76b0d2f1bbf32d32cdd8eb8c18/R/template.R#L60-L63

Is this something of interest for `pkgdown` or should I rather write my own wrapper around `pkgdown::init_site()`?

title: Vignette containing reexported S4 generic fails to render in `build_articles()` call
description:
I'm hitting an issue that I can't figure out how to troubleshoot, which is related to a reexported S4 generic. In my [bcbioRNASeq](https://github.com/acidgenomics/bcbioRNASeq) package, I'm reexporting the `sampleData()` generic from my [bioverbs](https://github.com/acidgenomics/bioverbs) package.

I call the `sampleData()` function in my [example vignette R Markdown](https://github.com/acidgenomics/bcbioRNASeq/blob/master/vignettes/bcbioRNASeq.Rmd), which knits correctly. The `sampleData()` function also passes `R CMD check` and other build checks. However, pkgdown is having trouble locating the function when attempting to link it during the `build_articles()` call -- see `pkgdown:::find_reexport_source()` step in the backtrace.

I'm only seeing this issue pop up with reexported S4 generics but not standard functions.

Here's the complete backtrace, for reference:

title: Rd tabular formating is mangled by `\code` calls in html output
description:
I ran into an issue where the formating conversion from *.Rd -> HTML gets confused in a **\tabular** environment within the *.Rd when a **\code** call is used in one (or many) of the elements (cells).
Here is a pseudo-`reprex`. The back-ticks are converted into **\code** elements by `roxygen2` (\code{b}) and this causes the issue. This should be a 2x2 table, but it results in a 3x2 table. When the \code is removed, everything is fine.
```
#' Foo
#'
#' A *tabular* test of `pkgdown`.
#'
#' @section: A Table
#' \tabular{lll}{
#'   a     \tab `b` \cr
#'   foo   \tab bar \cr
#' }
#' @param x A character string.
#' @export foo
foo <- function(x) print(x)
```
And the resulting HTML:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/25203086/49469063-c3c5be80-f7c3-11e8-8e9f-b4970589a58d.png)

The issue might(?) be traced to here:
```
# correct 2x2 table:
table <- '\\tabular{ll}{a \\tab b \\cr foo \\tab bar}'
pkgdown:::rd2html(table)

# incorrect 3x2 table:
table <- '\\tabular{ll}{a \\tab \\code{b} \\cr foo \\tab bar}'
pkgdown:::rd2html(table)
```

Note that a new line is generated between "a" and "b" when it shouldn't be.
This might be related to #348 or #630, but I don't think so. Or ... is this intentional and you should not have **\code** formatting inside elements of tables?

title: custom docmentation url of other packages

But some packages are not archived by www.rdocumentation.org. What about add an option like

```yaml
documentation:
  pkgdown:
    pkg: https://user.github.io/pkg
```

to specify that `pkg::foobar` should be linked to https://user.github.io/pkg/reference/foobar.html. (In the above example, `pkgdown:` means the documentation site is built by pkgdown, it tells how to generate url for specific function and enables future extensibility)

description:
I was looking for a way to skip building some (yet incomplete, therefore failing) vignettes.

description:

This, of course, threw an error when trying to `build_site()`. But the error was not helpful in determining what the issue was. Are you interested in improving the error message?

as_html.tag_url <- function(x, ...) {

}

title: Use PNG favicon instead of ICO
description:
I think it would be better to use PNG logos directly as favicons instead of converting them.

- This removes the dependency to `magick` and reduces code complexity.
- [PNG favicons are supported by all browsers (that use favicons at all)](https://caniuse.com/#feat=link-icon-png).
- 32x32 is way too small compared to nowadays standards and will probably look terrible on high-res retina screens.
- It may sound problematic to load a potentially heavy image file as favicon instead of a resized 32x32 img but most clients will cache it and it is already loaded in the body of `index.html` anyways.

If you agree, I can submit a PR with this change.

title: Links to GitHub ".md" files changing to links to non-existent ".html" equivilents
description:
For GitHub projects with a README.md (or README.Rmd) links that happen to link to ".md" files in the same GitHub project get converted from ".md" to ".html" during `pkgdown::build_site()` (and are thus broken as pkgdown is not in a position to produce those ".html" files).  This is happening to links that are not part of the doc-tree and thus should not be translated. My guess is pkgdown thinks these are links under its management (thinks they are pointing into the doc area and need to change to ".html") when they are links to un-related sections of the package/project.

Minimal example explaining the issue [here](https://github.com/JohnMount/BrokenLinkExample/blob/master/README.md).

A work-around is to relpace ".md" with "%2Emd" to hide the links from the processor.

title: templates/content-home.html is ignored if source is .Rmd
description:
When building the home page, the template content-home.html is only respected if the source is a .md or DESCRIPTION file. If it's index.Rmd or README.Rmd, the template content-article.html is used instead.

That caught me out whilst building a custom site with my own templates, and means the sidebar can't be removed from the home page without also removing it from all the articles.

The switch happens here:
https://github.com/r-lib/pkgdown/blob/master/R/build-home-index.R#L14-L26
and the call stack for .Rmd sources goes: `render_index()` > `build_rmarkdown_format()` > `rmarkdown_template()` > `render_page(pkg, "article", data)`

I've pushed a branch on my fork [here](https://github.com/goldingn/pkgdown/commit/439001cc0fe7d02a2a11b0e105c21f77d12870c3) with one passing test (for index.md) and one failing test (for index.Rmd) to demonstrate.

Let me know if you'd like that in a PR. Unfortunately I won't have time in the near future to send a fix.

2. Is there an option someone in the R code or yaml file to make this change?That is, is making this change in the output html the best way for me to make this change?

Thanks again for creating such a useful package.

title: Navbar highlighting is seemingly random in individual reference pages
description:
Dear developers,

What controls which element is highlighted in the navbar when a user navigates individual Reference pages? Taking a look at `pkgdown` itself, the [Reference index](https://pkgdown.r-lib.org/reference/index.html) correctly highlights "Reference" in the navbar. However, [individual reference pages](https://pkgdown.r-lib.org/reference/init_site.html) highlight the home button.

Looking at other packages, we find that [reference pages](https://aloy.github.io/qqplotr/reference/stat_pp_point.html) in `qqplotr` highlight "Articles". [Reference pages](https://artemsokolov.github.io/ABCmonster/reference/ABCcv.html) in my own package that I'm currently putting together seem to highlight yet another (custom) element called "Data".

This behavior appears somewhat arbitrary. Am I just missing an option somewhere? If not, I think the logical default behavior is to have individual reference pages continue highlighting "Reference" in the navbar.

Best,
-Artem

title: Reinstall package after updating the documentation
description:
We encountered a problem where the NAMESPACE file was not updated on the master (which is clearly our fault) which then uncovered some potentially unwanted behavior of `pkgdown`:

- Package is re-installed (https://travis-ci.org/mlr-org/mlr/jobs/388222642#L1199) while building the reference
- NAMESPACE is updated (https://travis-ci.org/mlr-org/mlr/jobs/388222642#L1221), package is re-loaded (not re-installed). 
- `pkgdown` starts a new R session via `callr` to build the html docs. We now get an exception as the new session picks up the package from the file system with the outdated NAMESPACE.

While it is clearly our responsibility to ensure that all functions are properly exported, I believe that working with two different versions of the package is unintended. IMHO `devtools::document()` should be called before re-installing the package.

title: Option to disable internet connections
description:
pkgdown connects to CRAN during the build process to check for:

- the package's existence there (https://github.com/r-lib/pkgdown/blob/master/R/build-home-index.R#L76)
- the package's release timeline (https://github.com/r-lib/pkgdown/blob/master/R/build-news.R#L161).

This causes build errors for users with limited internet connectivity (#762, #766).

Using `nslookup` is not ideal because even real connections might fail intermittently (#767).

We need a way to let users explicitly disable internet connections. This could be:

- A param (`internet = FALSE`) that is propagated through the build process.
- An user-defined option (#768) (e.g., `getOption(pkgdown.internet)`)

This flag would be checked by `build_news()` and `build_home_index()` before connecting to  CRAN.

title:
preserve custom classes (and other HTML?) in ...
in articles
description:
I ran into some funny/frustrating behavior of `pkgdown::build_article()` today. I have my own special html5 table, with its own HTML, css and js assets – which all work fine via `htmltools`, and inside a bunch of rmarkdown outputs. However, when rendered inside a vignette via `pkgdown::build_article()` my HTML goes to hell, because, as it turns out, [`pkgdown:::tweak_tables()`](https://github.com/r-lib/pkgdown/blob/580ec7462d640bc5b6b9a0d7d8ca2b500e602a17/R/html-tweak.R#L70) will **replace all existing classes**, and there seems to be no way to disable this behavior. So if you add the following plain HTML to some `vignette.Rmd`: ```
``` The class `foo` will disappear in the rendered `vignette.html` and be replaced by a (bootstrappy?) `css = "table"`. I'm not quite sure what the logic for this is, but I'm guessing streamlining the table layout. However, sometimes a *custom* table layout (as, perhaps, inside an HTMLWIDGET) should be retained. **Would it be possible to: *prepend* the css class `table` to any existing classes, rather than just delete it?** In general, I'm now worried that any of the other `tweak_html()` functions might have such unexpected consequences on custom styling (and js) I might have for htmlwidgets and such. Are there other potential dangers, and do you have a suggestion for how to avoid them? Perhaps some special syntax to mark HTML areas as "off limits" to any `tweak_html()`-magic?

title: Contents starts_with returns all pages if no matches
description:
Hi,

I've used prefixes on some of my package files to identify internal or unsafe (in development) functions. I've just transplanted my work from my first package into my second.

In my _pkgdown.yml I've put the following code chunk:

```
reference:
  - title: In progress / unsafe functions
    desc:  >
      Functions in this category are recognised as being important.
      However they haven't been fully tested, or their API or
      precise role within the code hasn't been determined so should
      not be part of the fixed code. They start with the name
      "unsafe" until they are more complete and/or tested.
    contents:
    - starts_with("unsafe_")

```
Interestingly I don't currently have any documented functions which begin with `unsafe_`.

Rather than returning no sections (expected behaviour given no matches), this appears to return all sections (including of course the ones we've already indexed).

It looks like a bug rather than intended behaviour.

Not sure whether expected behaviour would be to report an error in the code, or to put a 'there are no functions in this section' line into the output, or both (you can see in my example of an unreleased package in development documenting the functions that we know we'll need but are scrappy pre-conceptual things is quite useful, and knowing there are none of them in the index is valuable). 

Demonstrated on pkgdown 1.1.0 - but checking the changelog I can't see anything relating to this in the dev branch.

title: Strip fragment off GitHub URL before appending to it
description:
If a package has a GitHub URL like so: <https://github.com/tidyverse/reprex#readme> (note the trailing `#readme`), it creates dysfunctional links in pkgdown.

For example the `Source: R/reprex.R` link here:
<http://reprex.tidyverse.org/reference/reprex.html>
links to
<https://github.com/tidyverse/reprex#readme/blob/master/R/reprex.R>
which doesn't resolve and redirects to the top level of the repo.

This same problem is solved in usethis here:
https://github.com/r-lib/usethis/blob/3cc50ae7c4877d5f10747d0e8f25469897206cfe/R/browse.R#L93-L115

If we ever create [a package to parse Git remote URLs](https://github.com/r-lib/ghurl/issues), we'd be able to use that.

title: problem with build_home creating index.html when description field has a mix of quotes and brackets
description:
I encountered a problem with building a site where `build_home` creates mangled html in  `index.html`  when the `Description` field in the package DESCRIPTION file contains a mix of double quotes, single quotes and angle brackets for urls.   (example in package [statsr](https://github.com/StatsWithR/statsr/tree/BayesFactor) BayesFactor branch.)   If the placement of the quotes/angles and length is long enough it leaves spurious text that appears in the homepage.   In other cases it may leave blank lines above the title on the homepage.


The following  edited Description  field in the DESCRIPTION file can trigger the behavior when added to the `pkgdown` DESCRIPTION:  

``` 
Description:  Generate an attractive and useful website from a source 
  package using "pkgdown" <http://pkgdown.r-lib.org> convert your documentation, vignettes,
  "README" and more to  'HTML' making it easy to share information 
  about your package online.  See "Writing R Extensions" for help in
  formating the Description field.  Need single quotes for functions, 
  double quotes for titles of articles/books and 
  <http://pkgdown.r-lib.org> 
  angle  "<" ">" brackets for urls like 
  <https://github.com/r-lib/pkgdown>.  It seems to need a long enough
  package description to trigger the appearance of the mangled meta tag 
  for description and a 'random' mix of the different quotes and braces.
  Add this "description" to the 'pkgdown' files and then
  run 'build_home' to see the effect or look at
  output in "docs/index.html".
```

occurs with both pkgdown version 1.0.0 and 1.0.0.9000

title: Removal of `path` argument in `build_site`
description:
A recent commit (1ba293f394d852447e904b76bf4564edaef6afee) removed the `path` argument to `build_site` in favor of a `_pkgdown.yaml` setting called `destination`.

I think this decision has reduced flexibility of the package. Have I missed something? Here are a few thoughts on my use case for your consideration:

Out of principle, I keep only code that I want to version control in my git repository, and I try to keep automatically generated documents out of the repository. These auto-generated docs include things like the output of pkgdown. I do not want to commit them into the repository, because they clutter the commit history and repo size, and I do not need to version control them because they are derived from my version-controlled code.

Even without this issue, running the web pages like this increases overhead for authors with many R packages. I have written many R packages, each in its own git repository that I keep on GitHub. Because I have many R packages, each with a site generated by pkgdown, it makes sense to keep all of these web pages in a separate location which is served on the web, rather than maintaining a *pages* site for each repository individually.  Therefore, I want to point the output of `pkgdown` to this web-server location that is common for all my R packages and potentially other web items. This greatly simplifies the setup of new R package web page deploys, and also simplifies maintenance of web pages, templating, etc.

In the past, I wrote a simple command-line function that would build the `pkgdown` site in this shared space:

```
pkgdowngen () 
{ 
    R --quiet -e "pkgdown::build_site('${HOME}/code/$1', path='/path/to/www/$1')"
}
```

Upon updating an R package documentation, this one-liner would update the pkgdown-generated web page in a separate space, which is easy to maintain for dozens of packages. This workflow, which I view as the most efficient for using `pkgdown` for authors with many R packages, is now no longer possible.

The alternative is to change the `_pkgdown.yaml` file for each R package to add the `destination` attribute. This would restore my workflow, but this is problematic for 2 reasons: First, it requires *hard-coding* the `/path/to/www` variable now in each package, when that variable actually has nothing to do with the package, but with my current environmental setup for web development. In fact, this makes these packages generally unbuildable anywhere except on the place where I usually build. This has reduced the portability of the package and reduced the utility of `pkgdown`. Second, it has now duplicated the `/path/to/www` variable across many places, where it was previously sufficient to have that in one place, making it much easier to move things around.

Thus, from my perspective, I view the change as both philosophically and practically inferior to the way it was previously. I just wanted to add this perspective in case it sparks some thought. If there is another intended way to accomplish what I'm trying to do that I've missed, please let me know.

title: docsearch config JSON not in best format for Algolia
description:
Thanks to @jayhesselberth for all the work on docsearch functionality. Below are a few things from my experience using it and submitting my config JSON to Algolia. I think it would be a nice gesture to the Algolia folks to ensure pkgdown creates JSON that best matches their specifications so they don't get overwhelmed with a bunch of JSON configs that aren't exactly what they want. 

Small changes that needed to be made: 

 * Algolia asked that I keep `sitemap_urls` as an array even when I only had one element
 * Algolia also added back some elements (e.g. `nb_hits` and `conversation_id`) that `build_docsearch_json()` neglected to keep from the original JSON config they created for my site
 * `build_docsearch_json()` created a file called `"docsearch.json"`, but that is not unique to my package so I had to change the file name to `"my-package-name.json"` when I submitted the pull request. It would be nice to figure out the package name and then give it a `.json` extension for the docsearch file.

Here is the difference between what pkgdown created and what Algolia changed on their end: 
https://github.com/algolia/docsearch-configs/commit/3e8ea55bfadc6ed667801e3380a915c3773aa16f

Here is the pull request from my experience pull requesting the pkgdown config JSON: https://github.com/algolia/docsearch-configs/pull/389

title: ENOENT on copying files in vignettes subdirectory
description:
In a `crunch` package vignette, we load images from an [`images/` subdirectory of `vignettes/`](https://github.com/Crunch-io/rcrunch/tree/master/vignettes/images). These fail to copy to the built pkgdown site and halt the build:

```
Reading 'vignettes/subtotals.Rmd'
Writing 'articles/subtotals.html'
Error: [ENOENT] Failed to copy '/Users/neal.richardson/Documents/crunch/rcrunch/vignettes/images/manning_knowledge_subtotals.png' to '/Users/neal.richardson/Documents/crunch/rcrunch/docs/articles/images/manning_knowledge_subtotals.png': no such file or directory
```

This is similar to https://github.com/r-lib/pkgdown/issues/569 and https://github.com/r-lib/pkgdown/issues/570; and like said in #570, if you create the `images` subdirectory and retry, it completes successfully. Presumably `build_site()` should make sure this file copying doesn't fail the first time. 

The traceback points to `fs::file_copy()`:

```
7: copyfile_(path_expand(path), path_expand(new_path), isTRUE(overwrite))
6: file_copy(path(path_dir(input_path), ext_path), path(path_dir(output_path), 
       ext_path), overwrite = TRUE)
5: render_rmarkdown(pkg, input = input, output = output_file, output_format = format, 
       output_options = options, quiet = quiet)
4: .f(.x[[i]], ...)
3: purrr::walk(pkg$vignettes$name, build_article, pkg = pkg, quiet = quiet, 
       lazy = lazy)
2: build_articles(pkg, lazy = lazy, override = override, preview = FALSE)
1: pkgdown::build_site()
```

Given #569 / #570, this sounds like a general problem that could merit a general solution, so we might try to resolve this by wrapping `file_copy()` like this:

```
safe_file_copy <- function(path, new_path, ...) {
  fs::dir_create(unique(dirname(new_path)))
  fs::file_copy(path, new_path, ...)
}
```

to ensure that destination directories always exist before trying to copy. Alternatively, we could also just add the `dir_create()` inside `render_rmarkdown()` and fix it for vignettes. Happy to submit a PR that does either (or something else entirely); figured I'd file an issue and get guidance before going too far in one direction.

title: Quick arguments to suppress or rename homepage sidebar sections
description:
The default pkgdown behaviour -- to generate home page sidebar groups for Links, License, Developers, and "Dev status" -- is probably a good default, but not an exhaustive one. Users might reasonably want to suppress or rename some of these sections. Renaming has two major use cases: organizational (someone might want "Steering Committee" or some other header for Developers); and internationalization (individuals might reasonably want to translate their documentation websites). Finally, we can't change the order of these sections.

Currently it is possible to work around including dev status by having a separate README.Rmd for Github including badges and an index.Rmd for the pkgdown website excluding badges. But it is impossible to suppress the inclusion of the Links, License, or Developers sections, and impossible to rename any of them, and also a sub-optimal solution because it requires manually synchronizing content text between the two if they are otherwise identical.

In addition, because these sections contain no styling information, it is impossible to suppress sections with custom CSS. This means that anyone who wants to override these must do so by making custom templates (which pkgdown discourages and notes are poorly documented) or to manually edit the generated HTML.

At the risk of proliferating superfluous arguments, would you be open to a patch at some point that adds arguments to `build_site` and `build_home`, which would then pass-through to `tweak_homepage_html`, allowing users more flexibility than they currently have but less than a full custom template would require? I'm not sure how you would most prefer such arguments to be specified (one approach would be to give the argument "suppress_sidebar" which contains a character string or vector of character strings each specifying a section to suppress; another would be separate logical arguments for each section like suppress_license, suppress_developer).

In a similar spirit, a user might want to change the roles that populate the developers list depending on the package's internal organizational structure, so an argument like `populate_developers=c("cre", "aut", "fnd", "ctb")` might be well taken.

Thanks in advance.
