title: Sexpr issues: environment, working directory, multiple expressions
description:
Support for `\Sexpr{}` is currently rudimentary in **pkgdown**:

1. Each Sexpr is evaluated in its own environment inheriting from `globalenv()`,
https://github.com/r-lib/pkgdown/blob/897ffbc016549c11c4263cb5d1f6e9f5c99efb45/R/rd-html.R#L219
while `tools:::prepare_Rd()` uses a common environment for all Sexprs in a file (such that an Sexpr can depend on code evaluated in an earlier Sexpr).

2. The system Rd macros `\packageTitle`, `\packageDescription`, `\packageAuthor`, `\packageMaintainer` (which make use of Sexpr, see https://github.com/wch/r-source/blob/trunk/share/Rd/macros/system.Rd) assume the working directory to be the package root (where the DESCRIPTION lives). This is currently not guaranteed. The working directory is switched temporarily to evaluate the example code in `format_example_chunk()`, but not for Sexpr parsing.

3. A single Sexpr may contain multiple R expressions (such as `\Sexpr{x <- runif(100); mean(x)}`), but only the first one is currently evaluated (see `[[1]]` in the above code snippet) and returned. Why?

I think the first two issues are not straightforward to fix (by design), but maybe the third one is?

title: Parse usage section
description:
Enables:

* documentation & source lookup (#234)
* better listing on reference index (#256)

```
name(args)
x %name% y
name(args) <- values

\method{generic}{class}(args)
\method{[}{factor}(args)
\method{generic}{class}(arglist) <- value
```

`\S3method{}` is an alias for method; `\S4method{}` is used for S4 methods.

To parse, a reasonable strategy would be to replace `\S3method{x}{y}` with ``S3method(`x`, list(y))`` and then rely on `parse()`. Will have to do a little post processing if discover assignment. Then need to look up in the package namespace, using `get()`, `getS3method()`, and `getMethod()`.

title: package_rd() does not ignore non-Rd files
description:
The **fs** function `dir_ls()` is used to filter `.Rd` files as follows:
https://github.com/r-lib/pkgdown/blob/408dc8985028b7a95fb249ad44fad53eed198f58/R/package.r#L121

However, `fs::dir_ls()` ignores the `pattern` argument; the associated argument is named `regexp`. I stumbled upon this issue when I had an old `svn-commit.tmp~` inside `man/` which caused `as_pkgdown()` to fail with an "Error: Result 176 is not a length 1 atomic vector".

Note that `fs::dir_ls()` is used with an invalid `pattern` argument in two other **pkgdown** functions as well: `data_extras()` and `article_index_local()`.

BTW, I think `package_rd()` should employ a `[rR]d` pattern to also catch `.rd` files (this was not an issue previously since the `pattern` argument has been ignored).

title: build_home and build_news encoding issue
description:
This is following #339 
cc @antuki

There is an issue with encoding with `build_news` and `build_home` that do not render properly when building site on a french locale. Test 📦 is [COGuguaison](https://github.com/antuki/COGugaison) - a french one. 

`build_news` and `build_home` both parsed `.md`  file using an internal `markdown` function. It uses pandoc to convert markdown to html then makes changes in html using `xml2`, writes back the temp html file and then reads it line by line with `readLines` with no encoding provided.
The issue is here. 
https://github.com/r-lib/pkgdown/blob/05db627e5ebb9fde47b49b71f59e70acf41849c5/R/util.r#L58-L62

As `xml2::write_html` enforces UTF-8, readLines should assume UTF-8 input, but its default param is `encoding = "unknown") that assume the encoding based on `Sys.getlocale()`. On a french computer, it is not UTF-8 and the UTF8 html file is read misproperly.

Everything is working fine if I change to 
```r
lines <- readLines(tmp, warn = FALSE, encoding = "UTF-8")
```
or maybe more cleanly
```r
con <- file(tmp, encoding = "UTF-8")
lines <- readLines(con, warn = FALSE)
close(con)
```

I made the change in my fork. @antuki, you can try install to test on your system. 
```r
install_github("cderv/pkgdown@encoding-in-markdown")
``` 

Then I will make a PR if asked and if everything is fine after some checks. 

Question I still have: 

+ in COGuaison 📦 , all input file are saved as UTF8 which ease the process a lot. All the issue are because on system locale. I don't know how all this behave if file were not UTF-8 but latin-1
+ I can just test on french system but I assume it will work on others.

title: CITATION file rendering error: 'Error in if (!auto) { : argument is of length zero'
description:
## Issue 
If the CITATION file contains the call `citation(auto = meta)`, which is used by 
some R packages, the call `build_site()` stops with the error `Error in if (!auto) { : argument is of length zero`.  

## Reason
I tracked this issue back to the function `read_citation()` in 'build-home-citation.R':

```r
read_citation <- function(path = ".") {
  if (!has_citation(path)) {
    return(character())
  }
  path <- file.path(path, 'inst/CITATION')
  utils::readCitationFile(path)
}
```
It is basically the call `utils::readCitationFile(path)` which fails since `meta` is not a recognised object. In theory, the CITATION file itself could be changed to  `citation(package = 'packagename', auto = TRUE)`. This will work for 'pkgdown', but it will not work on CRAN. 

## Solution

I am struggling with a suggestion for a solution. It depends on what the package authors want. An obvious answer would be to remove the line  `citation(auto = meta)` in the CITATION file itself. Two reasons why this might be not the preferred solution:

*  Calling the object `meta` in the CITATION file is a documented example in the [R manual](https://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/R-exts.html#CITATION-files), means, it is something which appears to be allowed.
*  Apart from it, I think the problem is more general one: a failed call in the function `read_citation()` should not cause a full stop.

My suggestion, if something unexpected happened, a message and `character()` is returned. Or even better, the function falls back to `citation(package = 'packagename', auto = TRUE)` (and throws a message).

title: <doi:> references in the DESCRIPTION
description:
If the package does not contain an `index.[R]md` or `README.[R]md` file, `build_home()` falls back to the description field in the package's DESCRIPTION file:

https://github.com/r-lib/pkgdown/blob/c94e6b2d6ecc69c1a2e4093cd5736aa97dac94f9/R/build-home.R#L59

If this text contains `<doi:...>` (or `<arXiv:...>`) references, `build_site()` will currently fail with an error from `xml2::read_html()` in `update_homepage_html()` saying 

> Name doi:10.[...] is not XML Namespace compliant [202]

Dozens of scientific packages on CRAN use this DOI referencing feature, for example the [**party**](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=party) package (for a use case of `<arXiv:...>`, see for example [**palmtree**](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=palmtree)).

Ideally, `build_home()` should replace such DOIs and arXiv identifiers by hyperlinks just as on CRAN.

Similary, the description may contain direct weblinks given in angle brackets (`<http://...>`, as in, e.g., [**partykit**](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=partykit)), which are not parsed correctly (but do not break `build_site()`).

title: unknown system macros (\doi, \CRANpkg, ...)
description:
#287 has fixed the call of `tools::loadPkgRdMacros()` to be

https://github.com/r-lib/pkgdown/blob/c94e6b2d6ecc69c1a2e4093cd5736aa97dac94f9/R/rd.r#L9

The implementation of Rd macros has changed in R 3.3.0 (see https://github.com/wch/r-source/commit/10cb4e34cffd32aa6d0679d511f097f9ee373831). The second argument (`macros`) of `tools::loadPkgRdMacros()` now defaults to `NULL`, which means to load the system Rd macros from `file.path(R.home("share"), "Rd", "macros", "system.Rd")`. With the current value of `TRUE`, these are not loaded, resulting in "unknown macro" warnings when processing Rd files using macros such as `\doi` or `\CRANpkg`. Since **pkgdown** has `R >= 3.2.0` in its DESCRIPTION, a backwards-compatible fix is:

```
macros <- tools::loadPkgRdMacros(pkg_path, if (getRversion() < "3.3.0") TRUE) 
```

## Intended use

If I were to naively build the site on my company's systems, this output would include confidential information that I must not publish. `build_site(path = "docs", build_path = tempdir())` would make the precautions much easier.   Similarly to what happens when running `build_site()` I'd propose adding the possibility to automatically open a preview of the modified sections after running `build_home()` (opens index.html), `build_reference()` (opens reference/index.html), `build_articles()` (opens articles/index.html), etc... . It's a small thing, but it would allow quickly checking  changes without having to navigate to the appropriate /docs subfolder to  open the file manually in a browser. 

On a side note, since I'm not accustomed in contributing to other people's repositories: If I'd wish to make a PR to try to implement such a feature would it be better to first discuss it here (to see if it is of interest/makes sense), or should  I just make it and leave the maintainer to decide wheter to implement it ?

title: Use globalenv for rmarkdown rendering in build_home
description:
I have an issue with s3 dispatch in an rmarkdown chunk (in a readme). Consider something like

```r
point <- function(x, y) {
  stopifnot(is.numeric(x), is.numeric(y))
  structure(list(x = x, y = y), class = "point")
}

abs.point <- function(x) {
  sqrt(x$x ^ 2 + x$y ^ 2)
}

points <- mapply(point, runif(5), runif(5), SIMPLIFY = FALSE)

sapply(points, abs)
```

as a code chunk in an `.Rmd` file `README.Rmd`. Currently, `build_site()` will fail (or at least is does for me) with `non-numeric argument to mathematical function`.

As per suggestion by @gaborcsardi at r-lib/callr#33, this could be fixed by adding the argument `envir = globalenv()` to the `rmarkdown::render` call [here](https://github.com/r-lib/pkgdown/blob/d436a0ac943abbbb3a67dc2f6407116e4e458957/R/build-home.R#L74).

title: Incorrect link under "browse source code"
description:
The link created under the "Browse source code" heading links back to the site index, not the package's Github repo URL. For example, see the "Browse source code" link on this page http://hadley.github.io/pkgdown/

This issue occurs because the regex used in `data_link_github` (the last line shown below) captures both the site URL (e.g., "http://hadley.github.io/pkgdown/") and the repo URL (e.g., "https://github.com/hadley/pkgdown"):

https://github.com/hadley/pkgdown/blob/dd4635a1b8ac8418486c89c8ef0d85c54c52a76a/R/build-home.R#L191-L198

This can be fixed by changing `github <- grepl("github", urls)` to `github <- grepl("github\\.com", urls)`. A PR is on the way

library(Zelig)

title: Separate paragraphs are joined if text is indented
description:
I updated pkgdown to the current version on GitHub (my last version was from February 10, 2017) and since the update, the following issue occurs:


The code in the documentation looks as follows:
```
#' @references Text1
#'   
#'   Text2
#'   
#'   Text3
```


This is displayed in the R help as:

**References**

Text1

Text2

Text3


However, in the documentation created with pkgdown it is displayed as:

**References**

Text1 Text2 Text3


This seems to have to do with the indentation, because when the code above is changed to:

```
#' @references Text1
#' 
#' Text2
#' 
#' Text3
```

The result both for the R documentation and the documentation created with pkgdown is:

**References**

Text1

Text2

Text3

As far as I know, this issue has not occurred before the update, i.e., in the pkgdown version from February 10.

Best,

Pascal

title: Working directory when building index.html
description:
The working directory when building index.html is `docs/` but the source file (I've experimented with README.Rmd and index.Rmd) lives at the top-level. This creates the usual problems with file paths to, say, a token file or an embedded image.

I'm working around this by using rprojroot:

```{r, include = FALSE}
token_path <- rprojroot::find_package_root_file("tidyverse-noncaching-token.rds")
googledrive::drive_auth(token_path)
```
or

```{r out.width = '100%', echo = FALSE}
knitr::include_graphics(
  rprojroot::find_package_root_file("bacon.jpg")
)
```

I don't know if this is something to be fixed? Or a gotcha to be documented.

title: Rendering pkgdown fails if README.Rmd is a md_document
description:
Some `README.Rmd` contain the following header:

```
---
output:
  md_document:
    variant: markdown_github
---
```

But `rmarkdown::md_document()` doesn't have a `html_preview` option, and rendering the pkgdown now fails entirely. I did not think this through, #217 may have been a bad idea.

title: Help topic with-a-hyphen is problematic
description:
It is tricky to work with a help topic that contains a hyphen in `_pkgdown.yml`.

I've got one called `cell-specification` in readxl. It appears in a context like so:

```xml

  - title: "Describe a target rectangle"
    desc: >
      Flexible specification of cell rectangles.
    contents:
      - cell-specification
      - cell_rows
      - cell_cols
      - anchored
      - cell_limits
```

The above generates this error:

```
Building function reference -----------------------------------------------------
Error in eval(expr, envir, enclos) : object 'cell' not found
```

If I quote with backticks, I get this error:

```
Error in yaml.load(paste(readLines(input, encoding = "UTF-8"), collapse = "\n"),  : 
  Scanner error: while scanning for the next token at line 28, column 9found character that cannot start any token at line 28, column 9
```

If I quote with double quotes, I get the first error again.

If I quote with double quotes and, inside, backticks, that works!

```
  - title: "Describe a target rectangle"
    desc: >
      Flexible specification of cell rectangles.
    contents:
      - "`cell-specification`"
```

title: Allow other extensions for the NEWS file
description: According to the [Bioconductor rules regarding Bioconductor packages](http://master.bioconductor.org/packages/devel/bioc/vignettes/BiocCheck/inst/doc/BiocCheck.html#news-checks), the NEWS file should be either named `NEWS` or `NEWS.Rd`. title: options() leakage
description:
The readxl pkgdown site prints a lot of tibbles. I find that options such as `options(tibble.print_min = 4, tibble.print_max = 4)` "leak" from my current R session into `pkgdown::build_site()` and possibly from file to file within the site (?).

Reproduce by grabbing readxl source. Build the site. Commit or at least stage. Now execute with your favourite integer:

```r
options(tibble.print_min = 7, tibble.print_max = 7)
```

and build the site again.

title: Type of regex recognized by matches
description:
Thanks for the fantastic utility!

I am wondering what types of regex are supported by `matches` for the .yml config file to generate the reference index. I was trying to use negative lookbehind to selectively filter out functions, see here (want to match to PfSI but not SimBitePfSI): https://regex101.com/r/MZBNtT/1

The error was `invalid regular expression '(?<!SimBite)PfSI', reason 'Invalid regexp'` . Is there any way around this? Could the main functions pass down some parameters to `grepl`?

Thanks.

title: Rd tables mangled on conversion to html
description:
`as_html.tag_tabular()` inserts too many newlines when converting Rd `\tabular` sections to html. The following code should return a one-row two-column table, but instead returns a two-row, one column table (note the extra `` in the middle): ```r table <- '\\tabular{ll}{a \\tab b \\cr}' pkgdown:::rd2html(table) ``` ``` [1] "" "" "
a
b
" ``` The expected output is: ``` [1] "" "" "
a b
" ``` The culprit is [the first line of `as_html.tag_tabular()`](https://github.com/hadley/pkgdown/blob/master/R/rd-html.R#L236), which grabs the alignment characters. For some reason it drops the first one (the `[-1]`), so the alignment characters are converted from `ll` (two columns) to `l` (one column). The number of columns is determined form these, so everything is shoved into a single column. Here's a test that catches this: ```r table2 <- '\\tabular{ll}{a \\tab b \\cr}' out <- rd2html(table2) expect_equal(out, c("", "", "
a b
")) ```

description:

      toc_depth = 2,
      self_contained = FALSE,
      theme = NULL,
      template = path,
      dev = "svg"

```

title: parsing of help cross refs to other packages fails
description:
According to [R-exts](https://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/r-release/R-exts.html#Cross_002dreferences) 

```
\link[=terms.object]{terms}
```

should refer to the S3 "terms" class (in package stats). The relevant help topic is `terms.object` and the Rdocumentation url should be http://rdocumentation.org/packages/stats/topics/terms.object.

However this currently fails for at least two reasons, one trivial, the other more complicated
1. the trivial one see: https://github.com/hadley/pkgdown/commit/e356925a074411d71ba20c9ca518ceab0143e6a4#commitcomment-19581267
2. the complex one: `as_html.tag_link` currently assumes that if a link does not look like `\link[bar]{foo}` or `\link[pkg:bar]{foo}` then `foo` must be a topic in the current package. This assumption is not correct. In fact R-exts rather frowns on this form:

> There are two other forms of optional argument specified as \link[pkg]{foo} and \link[pkg:bar]{foo} to link to the package pkg, to files foo.html and bar.html respectively. These are rarely needed, perhaps to refer to not-yet-installed packages (but there the HTML help system will resolve the link at run time) or in the normally undesirable event that more than one package offers help on a topic83 (in which case the present package has precedence so this is only needed to refer to other packages)

For example if you take a look at the logic here: https://github.com/hadley/pkgdown/blob/master/R/rd-html.R#L106-L123 you'll see that `\link[=terms.object]{terms}` will always end up calling `link_local` whereas in fact what one needs to do is first look to see if the topic exists in the current package and then if it doesn't look for it in other packages. This will require quite a bit of mucking around with `as_html.tag_link`.

title: pkgdown assumes a package is on CRAN when in any repo
description:
If you create your own repo on your hard drive or anywhere not on CRAN, `build_home` sees it in `available.packages` and assumes your package is on CRAN. This means that the home page will say 

> Download from CRAN at https://​cran.r-project.org/​package=packagename

This can't be fixed in the `_pkgdown.yaml` file as that can only add links, not replace them.

title: build_home do not delete correct file with index.Rmd
description:
Hi, 

`build_home` first looks for index.Rmd or README.Rmd, then index.md or README.md. I think it is a great feature to have a README in github different from pkdown home page. 

However, inside the `build_home` function, it do not seems to work equally between `index.Rmd` and `rmarkdown.Rmd`. 

First, when `index.Rmd` is present, `index.md` and `index.html` are rendered. However, contrary to the case with `README.Rmd`, it is not delete because it tries to unlink `README.html`  in both case.  (see under). Same thing, message is not change between index or README.

I think `index.html` sould be deleted as well, as in the *README* case

Moreover, `index.md` is created in the working directory and not deleted but not useful I think. Is it intended ? 

The piece of code I am talking about, used with `README.Rmd` or `index.Rmd`

```r
if (identical(tools::file_ext(data$path), "Rmd")) {
    message("Updating README.md")
    rmarkdown::render(data$path, quiet = TRUE)
    unlink(file.path(pkg$path, "README.html"))
    input <- file.path(path, basename(data$path))
    file.copy(data$path, input)
    on.exit(unlink(input))
    render_rmd(pkg, input, "index.html", depth = depth, 
      data = data, toc = FALSE, strip_header = TRUE)
  }
```

All of the functions that it says "Can't find help topic ..." are functions created and used in examples. I _think_ this is somehow trying to generate help pages for functions created and used in examples - misreading them as exported functions? - (and failing since there's no documentation available). Obviously, we don't want these functions documented. While this doesn't seem to impact the final product (the website looks the same from the user's perspective), it does look like a bug...

I traced it back to [this commit](https://github.com/hadley/staticdocs/commit/4c7139bde2dccc85aa1b7a0c8433f05af62cba6e), in particlar, [this line](https://github.com/hadley/staticdocs/blob/master/R/highlight.r#L5):

try(expr <- utils::getParseData(parse(text = text, keep.source = TRUE)))
```

I don't quite understand the mechanism being used here (not super familiar with this part of the codebase)... Is there any reason why we'd ever want `keep.source = FALSE`. If not, the fix is obviously easy... But if there is a valid reason for that sometimes, maybe it should be an argument to `build_site`, or at the very least be left blank, so that the user can configure it using `options`, since the documentation for `parse` allows this: 

``` r
parse(file = "", n = NULL, text = NULL, prompt = "?",

      encoding = "unknown")

title: Add option to remove/ignore \dontrun when generating staticdocs pages?
description:
Hi Hadley, 

In almost all of our rOpenSci packages we make web API calls, and so our examples are almost all wrapped in \dontrun.  If we generate staticdocs pages, the examples then do not run. Is it possible to add an option in staticdocs to ignore \dontrun so that examples are run?

I wrote a little function to do this manually, but I'm sure you can come up with a much better solution:

nodontrun <- function(x) {
  dat <- readLines(x)
  dat[grep("@examples", dat)] <- "#' @examples"
  dat[grep("#' }", dat)] <- ""
  write(dat,  # change directory to one of interest
    paste("~newdirectory/R/", 
    x, sep=''))
}

files <- dir("pkgdirectory/R")
l_ply(files,  nodontrun) # which puts all .R files in a new directory

Then run roxygenize() (or document() ) on the .R files in that new directory

title: usage for s3 methods needs to include comment giving class name
Text of value section rendered as paragraphs rather than describe/dl
description:
According to "Writing R Extensions" > \value{...} > Description of the function's return value. > > If a list with multiple values is returned, you can use entries of the form > > ``` > \item{comp_i}{Description of comp_i.} > ``` > > for each component of the list returned. Optional text may precede56 this list (see for example the help for rle). Note that \value is implicitly a \describe environment, so that environment should not be used for listing components, just individual \item{}{} entries. However, they are not being rendered that way. An example is in `ggplot2::stat_summary`. The relevant section of the roxygen source: ``` r #' @return a data.frame with additional columns: #' \item{fun.data}{Complete summary function. Should take data frame as #' input and return data frame as output} #' \item{fun.ymin}{ymin summary function (should take numeric vector and #' return single number)} #' \item{fun.y}{y summary function (should take numeric vector and return #' single number)} #' \item{fun.ymax}{ymax summary function (should take numeric vector and #' return single number)} ``` The corresponding `.Rd` file: ``` \value{ a data.frame with additional columns: \item{fun.data}{Complete summary function. Should take data frame as input and return data frame as output} \item{fun.ymin}{ymin summary function (should take numeric vector and return single number)} \item{fun.y}{y summary function (should take numeric vector and return single number)} \item{fun.ymax}{ymax summary function (should take numeric vector and return single number)} } ``` The corresponding HTML (from http://docs.ggplot2.org/0.9.3/stat_summary.html) ``` html

Value

a data.frame with additional columns: fun.dataComplete summary function. Should take data frame as input and return data frame as output fun.yminymin summary function (should take numeric vector and return single number) fun.yy summary function (should take numeric vector and return single number) fun.ymaxymax summary function (should take numeric vector and return single number)

``` This is in contrast with the `\arguments` section which is similarly formatted in the `.Rd` file, but rendered in a `
`.

title: Problem with build_site()
description:
Not sure if this is a documentation or code issue.

I have just installed `staticdocs`. First port of call is `?staticdocs` which leads me to `build_site()`.

However this returns the error:

``` R
Error in if (file.exists(default)) return(default) : 
  argument is of length zero
```

Here's what's happening:
- `pkg_sd_path()` is returning `NULL` as the `staticdocs/` subdirectory hasn't been created
- therefore, in the call to `load_index()` we have `file.path.ci(NULL, "index.R")`
- which is a problem as this evaluates to `character(0)`

Creating the `staticdocs/` directory (where `pkg_sd_path()` expects it to be) solves this problem.
